items.title: Sister-in-law insists family don't need to bring side dishes to couple hosting Thanksgiving with 16 guests, host considers introducing sign-up sheet: 'I started cooking at 6 in the morning'
items.text:
Serving a full Thanksgiving spread by yourself is a challenge even for an accomplished chef, yet many non-cooks seem to think it's totally normal.

It's not that each separate component is necessarily that complicated; it's that timing everything correctly and knowing what to prepare in advance so that everything lands on the dinner table warm and ready is a logistical feat that is enough to overwhelm anybody. Add to that the astronomical cost of groceries and the time it takes to prepare a home for hosting, and it is kind of crazy to think of the number of people who expect that a designated female relative is going to be able to do it all single-handedly.

For this very reason, it is not uncommon for guests to help out whoever is on hosting duty with their own contributions. Maybe they cover the drinks, help clean the house, or bring a side dish or two. This holiday is all about being thankful for what we have, and that is much easier to do when people share the burden of the preparations, even if people aren't going to their house.

When it comes to the arguments and drama that tend to crop up around this time of the year, a lot of them revolve around one individual feeling like they are expected to do too much just so their family gets to enjoy themselves and celebrate. Unless you are explicitly told otherwise, it is pretty selfish to assume that one person can handle all the Thanksgiving preparations by themselves.

items.title: 'Good boys get good memes': 21 Dog Memes to Fill Your Morning Cup with Puppy Pawsitivity (November 5, 2026)
items.text:
It's that special time of the week again, and we're already barking with excitement over the new memes and laughs we have in store for today!

Whenever I'm feeling down on a random day, what always makes me feel better is a good dose of canine laughter and some puppy love to give me back my faith in humanity and that life can be beautiful.

Recently, I saw a video of a girl going to meet and pick up her new puppy girl for the first time. The poor thing had been abandoned and had spent some time bouncing around from one foster home to the other. This girl found out and wanted to adopt her, and all the arrangements were made. The thing was that the place where people were fostering her was like an hour away from where she lived, so her best friend went to pick her up and drove her and her new fluffy little friend around, no charge. Just two friends supporting one another and giving the little pup a new chance at a loving family and a warm home.

I usually watch a lot of rescue videos and read a lot of rescue stories. They are all unique and lovely, but what I loved the most about this one was the excitement and utter happiness that both girls were feeling. They wanted to help a little pup get the home she deserved, and they did. Their faces of complete love and tenderness are difficult to top, and they sure transmitted through the screen all their feelings and love for the animal kingdom. My mood after seeing them changed completely. I was so moved, and the whole story was so pawdorably perfect!

It was good that I saw that video when I did, because now I get to tell you about it while I share with you some of my favourite doggy memes to make you laugh and boost your good mood, just like that video did for me!

items.title: Friend brings unwanted date to dinner party for the host, gets upset when she rejects him: 'He handed me actual flowers'
items.text:
Why do people feel like they have to take responsibility for the relationship status of their friends?

Fun as it can be to gossip about relationships and dating, the love lives of our friends are only our business if they make them our business. Unless they ask for our help or explicitly accept the offer, playing matchmaker is often a risk that doesn't pay off. Just because you have decided that a certain person would be perfect for them doesn't mean that they will be.

Meeting a partner in real life is supposed to be making a comeback—if many singles are to be believed, the dating app fatigue is real enough that it makes the scariness of talking to people out in the wild more of a plausible option. There are plenty who are looking for love who would be delighted for a friend to introduce them to someone at a party or recommend an acquaintance who they think they would get along with. The key distinction, though, is that they have to be looking for a relationship. Despite what society tells us, it is not such a crazy idea to be happily single.

For those who are certain that they enjoy being on their own, any attempt to set them up is likely to be annoying to them. It is wise not to let the romcoms go to your head, and respect the way that they feel. If you don't, you might not just have a disagreement, but also disappoint another person as well.

items.title: 20+ Luxury Items ($1k-$10k) That Are Actually Worth the Money
items.text:
When you're shelling out for something, you probably want to make sure it's worth your money.

Everything is expensive nowadays. The Urban Institute reports that "Nearly half of people in American families cannot afford the true cost of living." This is a pretty bleak finding, but it rings true in most of our lives. It's expensive just to step out the door, let alone own anything nice. It can feel like you're always looking for the cheapest option in the short term. But sometimes short-term savings mean more money spent in the long term. I know this to be true in my own life. One thing you'll always need is toilet paper. And by my estimation, it's not the cheapest thing in the world, especially if you want one that is a little bit higher quality (which, in my mind, is worth it). But so often, when I would go to the store, I'd end up picking a smaller pack of it because I didn't feel like shelling out to buy in bulk. This isn't a smart decision, though, because it's so much cheaper to buy a lot, and it's not like you're not going to use it. You're going to go through the toilet paper no matter what, so you might as well buy in bulk. This is a lesson that comes with age and experience. You don't know this right out of the gate. When you're young, it's all about short-term decisions. But when you get a little bit older, you can start thinking in the long term. This is when the expensive purchases come in.

items.title: 22 Photos With a Weird Perspective That Make You Wonder If Your Eyes Are Working Correctly
items.text:
Sometimes imagination plays tricks on all of us, and we can't always trust what our eyes are showing us…

People usually say that 'you have to see it to believe it,' like you can't trust something unless you can corroborate it yourself and see it with your own eyes. Most of the time, they're right. We can't go about life just believing everything we're told without proof, but the mistake here is believing that our own eyes tell us the truth all the time. Newsflash: they don't. Nope, our brain and eyes sometimes get bored and decide to play pranks on us, leaving us more confused about how the world works than we already are.

I say this because of my own experience: my eyes get capricious and choose not to work. For reference, I wear glasses all the time and some days even with them on I have to double-check what I'm seeing. Of course, there are many things involved in how my eyes choose to behave on one day or another. If it's too late at night, if I'm tired, or if I was watching some sort of weird fantasy shows that were playing with my sanity, my vision becomes the least trustworthy thing in the room at that precise moment. So yeah, I've had my fair share of confusing moments when I think I'm seeing double, or that suddenly my cat can fly, but it turns out it's just a shadow. I'm not kidding, y'all. One day I was walking down the street going to the gym when I saw that further down the block there was a black cat all curled up in the middle of the sidewalk. I was thinking, 'Such irresponsible neighbors, how come they let their cat sleep on the street?' When I came closer, it turned out it wasn't a cat: it was a small pile of trash. That's how trustworthy my eyes are.

And on that note, you can imagine what kind of hilarious photos I have for you today. I want everybody to be as confused as I was, and you know, laugh a little as well.

items.title: After losing their beloved cat a family wishes for a ginger kitten and the Cat Distribution System brings them a new little bundle of love
items.text:
Only cat people can hear screaming coming from a trash can and somehow end up with a new family member! Most people take out the garbage and carry on with their day. Cat lovers come home with a kitten, a vet appointment, and a shopping list full of tiny toys. The Cat Distribution System has some questionable delivery methods, but we're not complaining!

The CDS seems to have a particular talent for finding people when they least expect it. You can spend weeks looking at adoption photos, trying to decide which kitty is right for you, only to have a scruffy little stranger appear out of nowhere and make the decision for you. Sometimes your future best friend doesn't arrive in a carrier. Sometimes he's sitting in yesterday's garbage.

That's exactly how one family in Greece met their newest little ginger. After losing their beloved soul cat two months earlier, they'd been hoping for an orange kitten. Then they heard cries coming from a trash can and discovered a hungry little floof inside.

His rescuers cleaned him up, arranged a vet visit, and planned to check the area for his mama or siblings. The vet estimated he was almost ten weeks old and a little underweight, but otherwise healthy.

Now, imagine the confusion of going from dumpster diving to being treated like royalty. Yesterday's menu was whatever scraps you could find. Today's special is Churu, served by your very own human staff. That's one heck of a promotion!

The little guy has already become a professional lap warmer, complete with a very loud complaint department whenever his humans leave the room. We suspect he'll be running the household before the week is over.

His new name is Gianni Purrsace, although Stinky Winky is also in the rotation. A luxury designer name for a former trash-can resident? We love a good glow-up!

Finding a kitten in an unexpected place isn't always the start of an easy journey. These little ones can need medical care, patience, and plenty of attention while they settle in. But watching a frightened stray discover soft blankets, regular meals, and people who adore him makes all that effort worthwhile.

Gianni won't replace the cat his family lost. He'll have his own quirks, favorite sleeping spots, and probably a long list of household rules he'll invent himself.

For now, this little garbage goblin has landed exactly where he belongs: somewhere safe, warm, and full of love.

items.title: Memorable Millennial Throwback Memes for a Magical Walk Through Memory Lane (November 5, 2026)
items.text:
Sit back, close your eyes, and enjoy this trip to the colorful 90s.

Do you have anything to share with your childhood self?

Now and then I get the uncontrollable urge to rewatch Full House and, with it, every other 90's sitcom ever made. There is something so special about going back to the TV format, vintage-looking, grainy picture, and funny-sounding era. In many ways, it feels like home. Like going back to when we were kids, Friday afternoon, turning on the TV and going on adventures with an unexpected family that always found a way. That was the highlight of our week. I know every generation says this, and all past times are better, but we really were privileged to grow up in a decade filled with good entertainment, colors, and fun all around.

I'm not saying things right now aren't fun. I do think that being an adult has a lot of upsides, despite the very clear downsides. That said, things used to be simpler. Fun wasn't about having thousands of followers or going viral, but it was as easy as downloading our favorite song from a very shady webpage, so we could listen to it on the family computer while looking at some very psychedelic patterns. Lying back and letting our minds ramble around imagination and creativity. That's what it was all about.

I know adulthood can feel a little hard sometimes, so quick back and enjoy a trip to the past; when we were kids, and our biggest worry was to not miss Full House's season finale. On the bright side, it's kind of cool that we are now very capable of understanding Joey, Jesse, and Danny, and finally realize how truly cool they were as grown-ups. Also, try not to think about the fact that the Olson twins are married and pay taxes. Let's focus on enjoying this excellent meme collection especially made for 90's kids.

items.title: 20 Tuxedo Cat Memes Proving You Can Wear a Suit and Still Be a Complete Goofball
items.text:
Oh, to be a tuxedo cat, looking fancy all day without ever having to worry about what to wear...

I have my cousin's wedding coming up this November, and I've already started thinking about what I'm going to wear. I need to find something nice, figure out what shoes to wear, make sure everything matches, and probably spend a long time getting ready on the actual day. Guests have to dress according to a colorful dress code, so I'm wearing a lilac dress. I already solved the most important part of the outfit; now all that's left is to find proper shoes that match and glamorous accessories to elevate the look.

Then I look at tuxedo cats and realize how unfair life can be. These little goofballs wake up every morning looking like they're ready to attend a wedding. They don't need to be trying on different outfits, and they surely don't worry about whether their shoes match. They were literally born ready for a black-tie event. And they don't even have anywhere to go! Imagine having a perfectly good tuxedo and using it to spend the entire afternoon sleeping on the couch. I envy them a little. Meanwhile, I'm trying to decide which pair of shoes will be comfortable enough to survive an entire evening of dancing. Because that's what really matters. A pair of shoes can be perfectly elegant, but if they won't let me dance, I'm not putting them on. I need shoes that align with my needs. And my needs involve dancing all night long.

items.title: The Best Heartwarmingly Wholesome Memes and Posts of the Week (November 5, 2026)
items.text:
We have now entered the time of year when the main priority is to feel cozy.

In order to achieve that humble aim, we are fortunate enough to have a wonderful tool at our fingertips: that is, the cultivation of wholesomeness. There is nothing more wholesome than curling up in front of a roaring fire with your loved ones, or even just with a good book and a tasty hot beverage of your choice. Going on a walk and appreciating the beautiful colors of fall, going apple picking, maybe even knitting something warm to wear if you are the crafty type—all of it is a legitimate way of cultivating those happy, wholesome feelings that we all need to have on a regular basis.

Of course, it is possible to be wholesome at any time of the year, but it makes a particular amount of sense right now. The holidays are just around the corner, and they are supposed to be the epitome of wholesomeness, and the nights are getting longer and more in need of a little light to keep us going. It doesn't always have to be some big, extravagant activity, either, as wholesome memes exist to help get us in the mood for all that is heartwarming. They don't need to be dependent on the season, and they aren't spending so much time thinking about the opinions of other people. They are just here to do good and raise a smile for anyone who happens to stumble upon them while scrolling.

items.title: NOvember Memes That Say Yes to Not Doing Anything for the Rest of These Cold Months While the Sunsets at 4 PM
items.text:
Has it already been a rough autumn for you? It has only been 42 days since the autumn equinox, and man, it has already been a roller coaster. We're barely halfway through! So what can we do to keep surviving instead of falling this fall? Might we recommend staying in, resting, and scrolling through relatable memes this November?

Yes, yes, we might: Welcome NOvember participants! October truly put us all in the grave with that Halloweekend, and we're not complaining! It was a lot of spooktacular fun. But now we are all tired. So freakin' tired. Like, it's only 3 PM, and I could go to bed right now, ya know? Plus, the sun is now setting by like 4:30 PM, and that isn't helping. So, let's all participate in NOvember and just say no: no to another party, no to drinks after work, and no to that early morning run. The rest of autumn is for resting. The leaves have fallen off the tree, the garden is barren, and the mornings are extra chilly. How can anybody expect you to be a baddie under these conditions? No, I will be home LOLing at memes until New Year's Eve, thank you very much.

items.title: Your Weekly Delivery of 23 Soft and Silly Kitten Memes for a Midweek Mood Boost (November 4, 2026)
items.text:
Who decided playing was something we were supposed to outgrow?

Kittens can easily find something to play with. It can be a toy, a piece of paper, a bug, something moving under a blanket. That's enough. We tend to expect that playfulness from kittens because they're little. Of course they want to play! But sometimes we get so used to connecting play with childhood that we forget how much we still enjoy it as adults.

I notice it when I get together with friends and someone brings out a game or suggests trying a silly challenge. We can be sitting around talking, and then we're paying attention to the rules, watching everyone's turn, and getting excited about winning or doing the challenge right. I might have been thinking about leaving soon, but now I need another round. I'm having fun.

There is research that gives me another reason to make room for this. In a study on adult playfulness, some adults spent a week doing exercises like writing down three playful moments from their day or finding a new way to be playful. The exercises increased playfulness and had short-term benefits for well-being. The study looked at building a playful attitude in everyday life rather than testing one particular game. So it can include more than sitting down with a board game. It can start with a joke with a friend, a silly challenge, or finding a way to make an ordinary task more fun.

items.title: Employee Promised Their Mom a Thanksgiving Visit After Working the Holiday the Last Two Years, Then a Coworker Asked Them to Swap Shifts So She Could Spend Thanksgiving With Her Kids—Their Boss Refuses to Intervene
items.text:
In an account shared with an online community, this employee presents a difficult situation where their coworker approached them demanding their day off on Thanksgiving, arguing that their time with their kids was more important than the employee's time with their family. This creates a delicate situation, and after their manager told the pair to "work it out" the employee has been left wondering… what exactly was there to work out.

Does having kids in the make one employee's time off request more important than the other?

In several different jobs, I've worked through holidays when family wanted me to be present. It's not a great experience.

On the one hand, you have an obligation to your employer, and the looming threat of being fired if you don't turn up. On the other hand, you have the expressed disappointment of your family for missing "another" holiday and valued time together. Although they say that they understand, and you know that they do, you can still feel the pressure of their silent wish that things would be different.

items.title: A D&D Party of 33 Pawladins, Clawrics, and Meowgicians Rolling for Initiative to Level Up Your Day
items.text:
If you're a D&D player who also raises a cat child, you know you can never exclude your feline friend from the game table.

I'm going to start a new D&D group with my friends very soon. They have four characters: an elemental sorcerer elf with a dark secret, a ranger dwarf who escapes the law, a barbarian orc lady who has no idea what's going on, and a human cleric healer who's got to be the group's mom. And I am the DM, master of the story and worldbuilding, and the host for our bi-weekly meetings. Oh, and I almost forgot… my cat, Cassie, is going to take care of the entertainment. No D&D session is boring when she's around - especially because she refuses to leave the game table once we play.

If you're like me, a D&D player or DM who also hosts their party in their cat's kingdom - I mean, your house - you already know how every game night goes. Your players arrive, and it doesn't matter if they have cats themselves, they have to act like cat people once they're through the door. They each greet your cat with pets and baby talk. When you order food, everyone has to pay the cat tax and give your cat a little snacky. And when you play - your cat must dominate the table, roll the dice even when it's not their turn, and move the miniatures around the map regardless of their place in the story. This is just cat law. What, you haven't read the Cat's Handbook?

Regardless of how much you try to de-cat-ify your D&D table, your cat will always be there. And believe me, we're not alone in this. I found the most adorable examples of fellow D&D players who share their cats' most audacious moments during game night. Miniatures, dice, maps, character sheets, DM screens - nothing is safe for the precious paws of your feline overlord.

items.title: 23 Memes to Push Through to the Weekend (November 5, 2026)
items.text:
Did you get tricked into thinking that it's Friday already?

Life should not be one long wait around for two days in the week when we can theoretically do what we want, but all too often it feels like that. Pour one out for those who work Saturdays and/or Sundays; they don't even get the advantage of gyms and grocery stores being quieter during weekday working hours anymore, thanks to all of those gosh-darned flexible working arrangements, and then they have to deal with the rest of us gloating about having the weekend to ourselves.

In a just world, we would be trying to make the most out of every day of the week, but between working, chores, childcare, and whatever else the average person has on their plate, that can seem to be near-impossible a lot of the time. You can optimize all you want, but the likelihood is that you are still waiting around for Friday evening like the rest of us if you are a normal 9-to-5er. It simply can't come fast enough.

The one benefit of existing in the current era is that there are more distractions than ever before to help us forget that the average working person is only allowed 48 hours per week off the clock. The internet is full of wonderful and free entertainment that both commiserates with our struggles, and maybe helps us to forget them for a little while. It is a winning combination that is hard to resist.

items.title: Tiny cream puppy peeks out of her new human's cozy carrier before arriving her forever home to toys by the Christmas tree: 'I love her so much already'
items.text:
How can we love someone so much before we even know them?

This human planning her "dream puppy" adoption and getting a cozy carrier all set up has made me think about how loved this puppy was even before getting adopted. Isn't that so sweet? Someone loved her even before she knew about it. Her human prepared a cozy bag for the puppy's first moments on the ride home, and not only that, but she also had toys waiting for her at home. It is clear how excited she is to bring her puppy into her life. All the anticipation and the excitement to take care of a new life make puppy adoption a real celebration, as it should always be. Every puppy deserves to be loved like this.

This event inevitably made me think of some friends of mine who recently became parents. I noticed that their baby, Simon, has made me feel something similar. They're the first close friends around my age to have a baby, so it's been a big moment for our group. We've shared so many things as friends (including playing together in the same band) that now getting to see them in this new part of their lives as parents makes me feel touched. What surprised me was how much we all already loved their baby before we even met him. People were getting together because of him, making room for him, buying things for him, wanting to know how everything was going when he wasn't even here yet.

items.title: 18 Rainy Day Memes to Smile Under The Water
items.text:
Rainy days can be a good excuse to stay in bed all day, but they can also be a bummer when you still have to go out.

I love a rainy day. Sleeping with the raindrops clashing on the roof and making noise, everything looking gloomy and grey, the smell of the grass getting wet. Or when you are in the passenger seat of a car, and it starts raining so you put your head against the car window and start to feel like in an Olivia Rodrigo music video. Having a valid excuse to cancel whatever plan, being able to skip school as a kid, being able to avoid cleaning the garden for another week. Rainy days are the best, especially when you are looking for excuses to avoid doing something. No matter what it is that you want to avoid, if it's raining, then that is a good enough excuse to avoid doing it, at least for that day.

Rainy days seem to be the best, but that is mostly if you are young, it's a weekend, or if you are a remote worker. When you are young, you can cry to your parents to stay home just because it's raining; it may not always work, but sometimes it does. When it's a weekend, a rainy weekend, then officially all your plans are canceled, and you can just stay home all weekend doing absolutely nothing. Order delivery, binge a TV show, sleep for 12 hours. Everything is possible. When you are a remote worker, whether it's raining or sunny, you don't really realise it; you are too busy working in your pajamas to look out the window at all, but if it's raining, then you can maybe feel an ambience that helps you not miss coming out of your house for days.

This is all amazing, but when you are an adult with an on-site job, things don't work that easily just because of rain. The weather isn't what defines if you go to work or not; your boss and the paycheck you receive do. So just because it looks like a disaster is happening out there, you still need to grab your keys and walk out of that door at 7 a.m. And I promise you, that is the worst feeling. Going somewhere when it's raining heavily outside feels like the worst day is happening. You have to carry a dumb umbrella or raincoat everywhere; you get wet everywhere, leaving a trail of water behind you. You come back home with your socks extremely wet and a cold forming inside your body. Everything is awful, and it doesn't seem to be getting better ever. So for those days when it's raining heavily outside and you still have to go to work, here are some memes you will actually laugh at, and I promise they can make you forget the unfortunate feeling of having to come out of your cave on a day that looks that bad.

items.title: 21 Orange Cat Memes Featuring Ginger Goofballs Waiting for Their Turn With the Brain Cell
items.text:
Have you ever looked at an orange cat and wondered what is going on inside that little head?

I have. And judging by the number of existing orange cat memes on the internet, I'm definitely not the only one. People often say all ginger cats share one single brain cell, and to be honest, oranges aren't exactly doing anything to prove it wrong. Some of the things I've seen them do make it hard to argue against it. But here's the thing: I actually know an orange cat who might be a little too smart for his own good. He's the exception to the rule. Ladies and gentlemen, I'll introduce you to Fred.

Fred is a ginger cat that belongs to a friend of mine and looks like Ed Sheeran. Yes, his face looks pretty much the same. What's so special about Fred? Well, he plays fetch. Yes, like a dog. You throw something, he goes after it, and he brings it back so you can do it all over again. The first time I heard about this, I thought it was hilarious. Since when do cats willingly bring things back to their humans? Most cats I've known would probably watch me throw a toy, look at me like I'd lost my mind and then look away, expecting me to go pick it up myself. So naturally, I have a theory. What if Fred has been hogging the orange cat brain cell all this time? Somewhere out there, another ginger cat is probably trying to figure out how to get down from a chair while Fred is busy mastering the rules of fetch. That would explain a lot.

items.title: ‘At first, I thought it was a fluffy white cat’: An albino porcupine is randomly seen crossing a road in Vermont, and it sparks comments about how cute it is from people on the internet
items.text:
The most surprising encounters with wildlife happen in the most unexpected places…

When we think about having a fortuitous encounter with wildlife, we always think we need to be in the middle of the forest or on a safari, but nope. Wild animals can spring at you in the most random moments and places. I don't mean to say that a lion is going to show up out of nowhere and try to eat you. For that, you would need to be in the middle of the savannah. But there are smaller, fluffier, and less dangerous wild animals out there that can show up on a random Tuesday to make your day more interesting. Which is exactly what happened to this couple!

They were driving in Vermont at the beginning of October when they saw a fluffy thing on the side of the road. They slowed down the car, obviously, and they saw the little creature cross right in front of them. At first they thought it was a cat, but it turned out it wasn't! It was an albino porcupine! You don't see that every day or on every road.

I can't even remember the last time in my life I saw a porcupine. In fact, I'm not even sure I have ever seen one in real life, just through pictures and videos, and for sure I had no idea there were albino porcupines in existence. Apparently, they are very rare; only 1 in 10.000 porcupines have that genetic mutation that prevents them from producing dark fur. They are definitely cute and look like a soft ball of wool. Mind you, they are still porcupines and still have those pointy spines, but we know ourselves by now: nothing could ever stop us from petting a cute little animal, not even the possibility of getting poked by one of those spines. We only hope that little buddy is okay out there, and that he has a long and happy life!

items.title: HR makes employees write thank you cards for coworkers about to be fired: 'They made us participate in firing our own coworkers without even telling us'
items.text:
There is no perfect way to let someone go, but there are a bunch of horrible ways to do it.

When you've been at a job for some time, you probably have some expectations about how you'd like to leave. Ideally, you'd do it on your own terms and sail off to a better job where you make more money. This isn't always the way it goes, though. Sometimes it's against your will, and there's not a lot you can do about it. But there are ways that you can soften the blow. The best way to do this is monetarily, of course. If you are in a position to give a good severance package, that can smooth over a lot of bad feelings, no matter what direction they're coming from. But if you're not able to do that, maybe there are ways you can make them feel good on their way out; that way there are no bad feelings in either direction. However, it's easy to go wrong when doing this kind of thing. That's what happened here in this workplace. A group of employees was asked to write letters thanking their coworkers for their service. What they didn't know, though, was what was going to happen next.

items.title: 'He Thought Halloween Was About Pretending to be Someone Else. He Never Realized He Spent the Rest of the Year Doing That': 17 Hopecore Memes to Kick Off the Workweek After Halloween on a Sweet, Hopeful Note
items.text:
The post-Halloween hangover. Why do I come up with my best costumes only after the party?

Now that Halloween is over, I come up with the best costume ideas. Of course, that had to happen the day after all the celebrations ended, right? Now I have to wait for an entire year to wear them, while they slowly become less funny or I simply forget them.

I don't know about you, but I never get invited to costume parties outside of Halloween, so I literally don't have any other occasions in which I could use my ideas. I guess I'll have to throw the parties myself or wait until next year. Meanwhile, I can channel all my frustration into decorating the house for the upcoming event: Christmas!

I know I haven't properly made it through half of November yet, but I need to get my hopes up, and at this point, anything will do. I've never thought about how much festivities keep us going, but they do.

There is something so cozy about turning your home into a little festive universe. Putting up decorations, hanging Christmas lights from the ceiling, and sipping hot chocolate next to an imaginary fireplace. I like turning my home into a little sanctuary that makes me forget I have eight hundred emails to answer ASAP.

This is exactly why I put together a weekly hopecore meme list, because I need this type of cute hope to keep me going until the end of the year. It's about allowing ourselves to get excited about the little things: a new holiday season, a cute outfit, hot chocolate next to an imaginary fireplace.

If we don't get excited about those things, what are we getting excited about? There are not many huge, life-altering events in life, so in the meantime, we should find reasons to be excited regardless.

So, as we power through another workweek, let this meme list be a reminder that, in life, not everything is about obligations, meetings, emails, and bills; some things are about holidays and cute little events and decorations!

I don't know about you, but I get pretty anxious around Christmas and New Year's, and I also like planning ahead for that reason. It gives me a sense of peace and control. If I plan and get myself ready for the event, it feels like I'm slowly digesting it.

After all, one has to accept that another year has passed and a lot has been left behind. The only cure for that nostalgic feeling is to be excited about the future and about it bringing more beautiful experiences.

So I hope you, like me, are decorating early this year. I love to see people who are committed to being excited and hopeful. The best is yet to come for all of us!

I wish you all the best as you tune in to that Christmas feeling that is already floating in the air. Maybe you'll meet the love of your life walking in the snow? Who knows!

items.text:
Remote jobs come with unexpected situations no one is ready for.

How to balance work etiquette and family life in a remote job?

Remote work comes with a whole new set of challenges, especially for people who live with their family, and even more if that family includes small kids. Even pets can become a factor you need to take into account when working from home, especially when you enter meetings that require you to have your camera on.

In this story, a remote worker struggles to balance important virtual meetings with family life. Their kids often interrupt those virtual encounters, and the married couple disagree as to how these interruptions should be handled. What would you do if this were you?

items.title: 'It feels like he sent his grandkids': After their 19-year-old black cat crosses the rainbow bridge, person says they're not ready to adopt, then two black kittens show up feeling like a sign from the universe
items.text:
Sometimes, the universe has a funny way of reminding us that love doesn't always end where we think it does.

Losing a cat is hard enough, but losing a cat who has been by your side for 19 years is a whole different kind of heartbreak. That's almost two decades of love, memories, routines, and all the little things that become such a big part of our lives without us even realizing it. And when you lose them, you're not just losing a pet. You're losing a family member, a little companion who's been there through so many different chapters of your life. I think that's one of the hardest things about loving cats so much. We know, unfortunately, that our time with them is limited, but knowing that doesn't make saying goodbye any easier. And after a loss like that, the thought of opening your heart to another cat can feel almost impossible.

I also think there's something very special about the way some people feel connected to the cats they've lost. Maybe it's a little sign from the universe, maybe it's the CDS working its mysterious ways, or maybe it's simply that the love we have for one cat makes us ready to love another, even when we don't think we are. And no, adopting another adorable cat will never replace the one we lost. It doesn't have to. There could be room for more than one little love in our hearts, even if it takes us some time to realize it. Sometimes, the CDS knows when we're ready, even before we do.

items.title: ‘The Memes Strike Back’: Star Wars memes for Rebels, Imperials and Force Users to Laugh at Across the Galaxy (November 4, 2026)
items.text:
Who's ready to go and take a trip around the galaxy of memes?

Lately I've been thinking about how much I miss watching the original movies. I've talked extensively about the prequels, but I hardly ever get into my favourite parts of the originals, and trust me, I have many. The beginning of episode 4, with Leia being taken hostage but still acting all sassy and fearless, like a proper princess, and figuring out her own rescue, is iconic to me. And so was her entering Jabba the Hutt's lair in disguise as a bounty hunter to rescue Han Solo, and finally ending Jabba all by herself. Queen behavior, if you ask me. Besides, it was obvious she had a thing for not letting anyone do what she could do herself, and frankly, I relate to that. We all know an eldest daughter type of girl who knows how to fend for herself. It was quite progressive, if you think about it, for a movie that came out in the seventies. She's a princess and a diplomat, but is never afraid to get her hands dirty when it's necessary. And she never stands still waiting for Han or Luke to rescue her. Yes, she was taken and locked up a few times, but every single time she managed to find a weapon and defend herself, and ultimately, find the way to escape for her and all of her companions. Is it too obvious that she's one of my favourite characters?

Still, she's not the only one who made an impact on me. Both Skywalker siblings were amazing in their own way. All the moments in which Luke had to put his Jedi training to the test were also awesome, mostly because he didn't just turn into an expert after one training session. Even after Yoda taught him all that he could and Luke was feeling confident, he still had to go out and try, fight two Sith who were more powerful than him, fail, and try again. I liked that about the originals: he had to work hard to become powerful, even with a natural inclination to use the Force, which made the character feel all the more real.

items.title: 27 Food Memes to Scroll Through While Eating a Much-Needed Snack
items.text:
Someone's gotta eat all the leftover candy from Halloween, and we are happy to volunteer.

Are you thinking about your next snack right now?

With Halloween season over, you probably have lots of candy bags around the house. For some, it's what's left after trick-or-treating with the children, and for others (like me), it's the leftovers of a celebration that consists of indulging in treats you don't usually eat. It's part of the Halloween spirit: get some candy for your family and friends, so you can have an excuse to also get some for yourself. And what better moment to take those bags out and start digging through whatever is left?

You're probably working right now. Going through the motions of the day, trying not to get too distracted. But when your stomach starts making horror movie noises, it's time to take a break and have a snack. In the meantime, here's a hilarious food memes collection that will make you even more hungry. Pro tip: you can scroll through it as you have a delicious morning break. May I suggest a classic? Coffee and donuts never disappoint, or, if you're more of a savory type of person, a well-made sandwich will hit the spot as it always does. Bon appétit!

items.title: A Nutty Little Batch of Squirrel Memes to Start November With a Silly Snack Break
items.text:
Would squirrels agree that the snacks are the most important part of planning any gathering?

Just like squirrels, I need to plan the snacks first. So yesterday I started November with a good stash of snacks! I had some friends over at my place for a movie night, and the first thing we decided was what we were going to eat. We hadn't picked the movie yet. That could wait. I had to make sure there would be brownies and popcorn first. And then we also got pizza. (The sweet snacks were all that mattered, actually)

I'm like a kid with money. I could buy chocolate for dinner and no one would object, since I live alone.

items.title: Georgia pet owners discover via Facebook that the Pug and 19-year-old cat they paid to euthanize are alive and secretly living with the veterinary staff
items.text:
They said their goodbyes, paid the bill, and went home to grieve. Months later, a Facebook post showed them their "late" pets were very much alive, and living with the people they'd trusted to put them to rest.

We all want more time with our pets. Those 10, 15 years (20, if you're lucky) pass too quickly. But eventually, every pet owner has to face the same problem at some point: making the decision to put your pet down. It's one of the hardest decisions a pet parent has to make.

Then, after the decision, comes the dreaded drive to the vet's office to lay them to rest. You give them all their favorite foods, tell them every minute how much you love them, and you try to make them as comfortable as possible. In this very vulnerable state, you're trusting the veterinarians to do their job and help you let go. Or so you think.

In Senoia, Georgia, two pet owners were scrolling through Facebook, when they found their sick Pug and 19-year-old cat, whom they had brought to be euthanized months ago, alive. They were living with the vet staff, who took their money for the procedure, but never followed through with it. They secretly kept the animals alive, deciding on their own that they should be given more time to live.

What would you do if you found your "deceased" pet alive from a photo on Facebook?

items.title: 27 Hilarious Memes to Turn Your Midweek Slump Into a Wednesday Comedy Club
items.text:
How about another cup of coffee and some funny memes to get over Wednesday?

Am I the only one who puts personalities into the days of the week? Okay, let me explain. Have you ever talked to someone about how certain days give certain color vibes and have a specific personality? For example: Monday is red and is similar to a Math teacher. It gives that hard-to-get-through, complicated vibe. When it comes to Wednesday, I've always associated it with good, positive energy, for some reason. But I realized that I'm the only one! Most people I've talked to struggle a lot on Wednesday because you still have two days until the weekend and three more days of work. I understand the concept, but it's the middle of the week! The two worst days are over, and now we're starting to feel some happiness and relaxation return to our bodies.

Since most people aren't like me and need some sort of pick-me-up to get through Wednesday, I have selected some good and funny memes for you. Instead of reaching for coffee and giving your body a caffeine break, let's dive into some good old internet comedy, which I'm sure will give you the joy you're looking for.

items.title: A Floptastic Collection Of Doggos With Giant Ears And Tiny Attention Spans
items.text:
Some dogs have ears bigger than their heads, yet somehow they can't hear a single thing their humans say. Unless there's food involved. Then their hearing works just fine!

Every dog pawrent knows the struggle of calling their pup's name approximately twenty times before getting any acknowledgment. You could be standing right beside them, waving your arms and practically begging for their attention, and they'll continue staring at a squirrel. But whisper the word "treat" from another room, and suddenly they're listening!

We're convinced dogs understand a lot more than they let on. They know exactly what "walk" means, recognize the sound of their food bowls, and can hear a cheese wrapper opening from the other side of the house. Yet the moment you ask them to stop barking at the mailman, they act like they've never heard a human voice before.

The bigger the ears, the more suspicious we become. How can a dog have two enormous flappers hanging off its head and still ignore the person responsible for feeding it? Some of these pups look like they could hear a biscuit hit the floor three streets away, but "come here" is apparently beyond their capabilities.

Perhaps they've simply decided that listening is optional. After all, what's the worst that could happen? Their human calls them inside, they ignore the request, and five minutes later that same human comes outside with a treat. Sounds like a pretty successful negotiation from the dog's perspective!

Then there's the selective hearing that happens when it's time for a bath. Mention the word "bathroom," and your pup disappears beneath the bed. Ask them to come out, and suddenly they're fast asleep. It's amazing how quickly a dog can lose its hearing when shampoo enters the conversation.

We also love how they pretend not to notice when they're doing something naughty. They'll be halfway through stealing a sandwich off the counter, hear you say their name, and keep going. Maybe if they don't make eye contact, the rules don't apply!

The real talent is pretending they haven't heard you while their ears are actively moving toward your voice. Those little traitors give the whole game away! We can see you listening, buddy. You're not fooling anyone.

Of course, the second you stop calling and sit down to eat something, your dog suddenly remembers you exist. Now they're beside you, ears perked up, waiting patiently for a bite.

So enjoy these big-eared pups who've mastered the fine art of hearing everything and obeying absolutely nothing.

items.title: A Mouthful of Hilarious Cooking Memes for Amateur Chefs (November 4, 2026)
items.text:
Nothing beats looking forward to what you're going to make for dinner tonight.

Even better is when you already have the leftovers in the fridge, and all you have to do is heat them up. One of the simplest ways to feel a little happiness without too much effort is by cooking an easy, well-loved recipe for ourselves; there is a reason that they call it comfort food.

Knowing how to cook isn't just a valuable skill. Many would argue it is essential if you want to live a successful independent life. While it may be possible to live on takeout if you don't care about your budget or your health, there is something very beneficial about using your brain to figure out what can be made with the remaining handful of ingredients in the cupboard the day before your next big grocery shop. In a world where we are told to prioritize convenience, it is good to try to be resourceful instead.

That isn't to say that cooking always has to be about being sensible and saving money. Depending on the recipe or the occasion, a home-cooked feast can turn out to be mighty extravagant as well. We only need to look to the upcoming Thanksgiving holiday to be reminded of that. The great thing about learning to cook is that you can make food whatever you want it to be, so long as you have the patience and dedication. Considering that you can make many delicious meals in under 30 minutes, even that doesn't have to be too hard.

items.title: The Great Breakfast Meowtiny: Hungry Cat Memes and Daylight Saving Chaos
items.text:
Daylight saving time ended this week, which means we all got an extra hour of sleep. Just kidding! Anyone with a cat knows that extra hour was a complete scam. The clocks went back, but our hungry little gremlins are still demanding breakfast at the exact same time. Apparently, nobody consulted the feline community before making this decision, and they're absolutely furious.

Imagine being a cat. You've spent months training your human to serve breakfast at precisely 6 a.m. Then, overnight, this incompetent employee decides to make you wait another hour. Unacceptable! You'd be filing a formal complaint with management, too, if you weren't already busy screaming directly into someone's ear.

Cat pawrents have probably spent the past few mornings being rudely awakened by a furry face hovering inches above their own. Maybe it starts with a polite little meow. Maybe there's a paw gently tapping your cheek. Either way, the situation quickly escalates when breakfast doesn't magically appear.

You may as well replace your alarm sound with meows because cats will sing the song of their people for hours until you arise. It may start as quiet meows, but give it ten minutes and it'll reach a crescendo that could wake the whole neighborhood. And there's no snooze button on cats with full lung capacity. Putting a pillow over your head won't help when your opera singer decides to perform right next to your ear.

Don't even think about pretending to be asleep. Cats have all morning to conduct their little hunger protests. They'll sit on your chest, breathe directly into your nostrils, and stare at you until you crack. You're lying there wondering why you willingly adopted an animal who treats you like a slave.

The worst part? Sometimes the food bowl isn't even empty! There's still a perfectly respectable amount of kibble sitting around the edges, but your purrecious little angel has decided those pieces are no longer edible. Better get up and shake the bowl before someone calls animal control.

We'd love to explain that daylight saving time has ended and breakfast is now scheduled for an hour later, but negotiating with cats is a losing battle. They've never cared about our schedules, and they're certainly not starting now. As far as they're concerned, the only clock that matters is the one in their stomach.

So much for enjoying that extra hour of sleep. Our cats have officially rejected the time change, and we're just going to have to live with it.

Fall back? More like get up and fill the food bowl!

items.title: A Cozy Rainy Day in Dog Memes for Warm Hearts and Wet Noses
items.text:
Hola amigo doggos, we hope you have a great day.

So this summer remember that amigo doggos bring you muy buenos days, so if you want a better Sunday you'll be sure to scroll these doggo memes.

items.title: 'Life Lately': 17 Gym Memes for Eternal Bulkers Who Can't Stop Eating
items.text:
Anyone out there who hasn't been to the gym in the last two weeks?

I know I haven't. Look, it's been tough, okay? And I haven't been able to get my life back on track just yet. I might need some extra time to deal with everything I'm behind on; then I can go back to the gym.

This never happens to me; usually, I'm very disciplined, and it only takes me like one or two days tops to go back to my routine, but these past weeks, life has been hectic. I've been trying to keep up with all my responsibilities from work and studies, and even though I always manage to deliver everything, I'm always slightly behind. My schedules are messy, and I feel like I am all over the place.

Maybe this is denial speaking, or some kind of defensive excuse, but I want to get up to date with all my work so I can get back to my normal routine and stop dragging this mess through the rest of the month.

I promise I'm going back tomorrow, even if it's only to do some light cardio. The key is to go back; after that, readjusting is easy. It's crazy how little time it takes to get disaccustomed to something hard you used to do every day. It does get easier while you're at it, but the minute you stop, it's super hard to go back.

I think the best I can do is not punish myself for this; otherwise I'll make going back even harder, but I don't feel good about myself at all. And also, I kinda feel like my body wants to spend more energy than it's currently spending.

I have another confession to make: Not only did I skip the gym for two weeks, but I've also been eating carbs like there's no tomorrow. I think something inside me wanted to let loose, and I've decided to let it. I've said it before: I can't live my life restricting everything. I even believe restriction is what got me here in the first place. So I might have to use this time off to rethink my relationship with food and the gym.

Suddenly, the weights I used to comfortably lift feel intimidating, and I don't know if I can manage, but I suppose it's just a feeling, and it's only a matter of attitude. I hate that my muscles have forgotten how to work out, but my gut hasn't forgotten how to crave three thousand calories of carbs. It's not fair.

I accept it; I've failed, but beware, because when I come back, it'll be over for all of you. I've recharged all my batteries, and I'm feeling more motivated than ever. I will come back with more energy than ever, ready to pull off six more months of uninterrupted activity, and achieve the greatest physique ever known to mankind.

For this, I simply have to forget the love of my life: Gnoccis.

items.title: Chicago O'Hare traveler rescues stray kitten outside the airport, Door Dashes a pet carrier, and boards his flight home with one extra fluffy passenger
items.text:
The Cat Distribution System works in meowsterious ways, and for one traveler, all it took was a smoke break at Chicago's O'Hare Airport and a missed connecting flight to turn his unexpected delay into an even more unexpected adoption.

Depending on where you're going to (or where you're coming from), traveling with pets can be an enormous hassle. You need an airline-approved pet carrier, usually some sort of documentation and medical history for the animal, and a lot of patience. If the animal is small enough to come with you in the cabin, that's the best option, but if not, they have to fly underneath the plane in the cargo section, which comes with its own potential problems. This process can take anywhere from weeks to months. Now, imagine having to do it all in a few hours before your flight!

After missing his connecting flight at Chicago's O'Hare airport, Virgil Wiebe went outside for a smoke break. He found a small garden and started contemplating what to do with his remaining time before his next flight, when all of a sudden, he heard some tiny, distressed meows coming from somewhere around him. Then, out popped a tiny, 3-week-old orange kitten, all alone. Virgil searched for a mama cat, but alas, the poor kitty was flying solo (pun intended).

Well, what would any rational purrson do when finding an abandoned kitten with only a few hours until their next flight? Obviously, he couldn't just leave the kitten there, so he Door Dashed an airline pet carrier and kitten formula, got everything settled with United Airlines and booked one more ticket for his tiny, fluffy passenger, who he named Macanudo O'Hare, or Harry, for short. His layover/kitten rescue mission was now complete.

Travelers, if you thought that the Cat Distribution System couldn't reach you at the airport, think again! The CDS is all-knowing, all-powerful, and even if you're about to board your plane, you might just be expected to take a seriously smol (and seriously cute) rescue cat with you.

items.title: 'My face 90% of the day': 17 Antisocial Memes for Introverts Who Absolutely Love Staying Inside And Not Texting Back
items.text:
I've reached a new concept: Eventual Extroversion

Why do we have to categorise our personalities so much? Can't we be stable in some form of instability? Like knowing that once in a while we step out of our comfort zone and become extroverted for an entire weekend and then go back to normal? Is that not possible? Do we have to behave the same way always? Can't variations be part of our identity? Does that defy the concept of identity, or do we have an extremely rigid concept of what identity really is?

I'm not necessarily an introvert, but I'm definitely not an extrovert who has been repressing her socializing instincts. My desire to socialize comes in waves, and I love coming back home after a particularly sociable weekend and enjoying a full 4 days of not going out whatsoever.

I can't miss my own company if I don't go out, and vice versa; I can't miss anyone if I don't stay home for a few days.

I like staying home during the week, enjoying my time alone and planning for the weekend, and after an agitated weekend, there is nothing better than coming home and realizing how quiet and peaceful it is. I don't mean to go out every weekend; I'm just saying this for weekends that I do.

I like the concept of eventual extroversion because it allows me to talk about the fact that it's not that those of us who conform to that group have social anxiety or are antisocial; maybe we just like to alternate between going out and staying home.

Liking to go out once in a while is similar to loving chocolate cake; I can assure you'd hate it if you had to eat it for every meal. Why can't we treat extroversion the same way? Do we really have to act the same every day? I know my energy fluctuates, and my inclinations fluctuate with her. I like respecting that.

I just want to say neither version is more authentic than the other; that's why I came up with the concept in the first place. My appreciation for solitude grows exponentially every time I go out, and I like the feeling.

Every time I go back to my confinement, I rediscover my solitary activities with more excitement, and sometimes I even come up with new ones; for example, the last time I went out, I decided I wanted to create a LIVING GEOPOLITICAL WORLD MAP, because I overheard some people talking about some events I hadn't heard of, and it seemed like a fun way to keep up to date with the news, lol.

Can you imagine? A physical map with coloured pins and Post-its that represent the different governments and situations happening, a map you can update every time something new happens.

It might sound boring and geeky to you, but to me, it sounds like a wonderful game that I can play all by myself! And it reinvents itself! Bliss.

items.title: Bookseller faces pushback after criticizing customer for using ChatGPT to inscribe baby shower gift: 'Maybe this woman was going through a lot'
items.text:
Was she out of her depth, or just feeling lazy?

It is common for critics of AI to point out that it is kind of worrying that a lot of people who use these services seem to bypass using them for the boring, repetitive stuff and go straight to automating all of the things that require creativity, thought, and emotion. Artificial intelligence is probably here to stay, and it has some genuinely positive uses! However, those that involve trying to replicate the human creative process remain controversial.

As somebody who has loved words all my life, it is kind of incomprehensible to me that people would want to rely on AI to give them the words they need for everything from writing emails to wedding vows. Still, it is a task that many would prefer to outsource instead of putting in the work themselves. What it lacks in a personal touch, it makes up for in convenience. Writer's block is bad enough when you actually enjoy writing, let alone when you have always found it to be a chore.

Still, it is good to do things that challenge us now and again instead of taking the easy way out all the time. Arguably, this is also one of the main arguments against the current application of AI. Being able to write a couple of sentences is a pretty basic skill, and it doesn't say anything positive if somebody insists on avoiding it by any means necessary. We can't forget our capabilities.

items.title: Tolkien Tuesday: The Best Lord of the Rings Memes This Week (November 3, 2026)
items.text:
Much like Frodo's epic journey to Mount Doom to destroy the One Ring, meme-making is a quest that many Lord of the Rings fans feel like they have no choice but to undertake.

Unlike Frodo, though, they don't hope to get rid of this thing that they find so strangely beguiling. Tolkien-inspired memes can inspire a possessiveness of sorts in the fandom, in the sense that they are a product of their dedication to the cause that is frequently celebrated even by those who are not complete LOTR obsessives. At the same time, they get so much enjoyment out of making stupid jokes using scenes that they have watched a hundred times over that they are unlikely to be all that bothered when one of their memes breaches containment.

While Tolkien was a man of many talents, it is fair to say that he probably couldn't predict how a bunch of people riffing on some of his most famous works would become a bona fide cultural phenomenon. Yet the movies based on his books have remained culturally relevant not just because they are timeless classics, but also because they have been painstakingly memed, frame by frame (some scenes more notorious than others). A lesser series might buckle under the weight of all this humor, but it only seems to make the public appreciation for LOTR even stronger. The tale that it tells and the way it can somehow be applied to every single kind of everyday situation remain a crowd-pleaser that shows no signs of slowing down.

items.title: 'When was the movie better than the book?': The internet shares their opinions about terrible books that were turned into iconic movies
items.text:
I bet you didn't know that some of your favourite movies were originally books…

As a certified bookworm that I am, it's virtually impossible to convince me of the fact that a movie based on a book can be better than its source material, but like with everything in life, there are exceptions.

Most of the time, when I find out that a book I like is being turned into a movie or TV show, my first reaction is to say, 'Oh no, they're gonna mess it up big time,' and that's because, 9 out of 10 times, they actually do. Writers and producers tend to make unnecessary changes, misinterpret or misrepresent the characters, forget key parts of the plotline, and sometimes just make things up as they go, ruining an otherwise well-established story. The casting is a completely different topic, and it's not even worth delving into it.

However, on rare occasions, it looks like all the planets of the solar system align and movie producers actually set out to do their jobs right when adapting a literary piece, respecting the spirit of the source material and making an accurate and sometimes even better representation of the same story. It doesn't happen very often, but when it does, it's worth applauding it. Besides, I have to acknowledge the fact that, just like there are mediocre movies, there are also mediocre books, as much as it pains me to say it. These screenplay writers sometimes have the ability to take all the good stuff from an apparently irrelevant comic book or novel and turn it into a fantastic work of fiction. I have to give credit where credit is due, and in most of these cases, a round of applause is well deserved. So much so that I had no idea some of these were actually books.

items.title: Pawsitively Pawsh Kitties Serving Fall Furshion In Their Cutest Sweaters
items.text:
Sweater weather is officially here, and some very fashionable felines are taking their fall wardrobes seriously! Tiny knitted sweaters, cozy cardigans, and little scarves are making an appearance, and we're completely obsessed. Who knew a cat wearing a turtleneck could look more put together than we do on most days?

Getting dressed for fall is already half the fun of the season. We love pulling out our favorite sweaters, wearing fuzzy socks, and finding any excuse to get cozy. But seeing a kitty dressed in a miniature version of something we'd actually wear? That's a whole new level of adorable.

Just imagine opening your closet and finding your cat has better knitwear than you. They've got a lovely little cable-knit sweater, perhaps a matching scarf, and absolutely nowhere important to be. Their biggest plans for the afternoon involve napping on the couch and watching birds through the window. Yet somehow, they're dressed like they're heading to a fancy autumn brunch.

Of course, anyone who's tried dressing up a cat knows that not every feline is interested in becoming a fashion icon. You can spend ages picking out the cutest outfit, only to discover that your kitty would rather wrestle with the sweater than wear it. The look of betrayal alone could make you reconsider your entire career as a feline stylist.

For the cats who genuinely enjoy getting dressed up, though, the results are ridiculously cute. A tiny sweater makes an already fluffy kitty look even more huggable, especially when they're curled up on a blanket with their little paws tucked underneath them. Add a pumpkin in the background, and you've got the purrfect fall photoshoot.

We also love how much personality comes through in these outfits. A cat wearing a bow tie looks like he's about to give an important presentation. Put that same kitty in a chunky cardigan, and he's suddenly a retired purrfessor enjoying a quiet weekend in the countryside. One wardrobe change, two completely different careers!

Naturally, plenty of cats prefer sticking with the fur coats they were born with, and that's perfectly fine. Dressing up should be comfortable and enjoyable for the kitty, too.

Until then, we'll be admiring these stylish little fluffballs and wondering where we can find sweaters half as cute as theirs. Move over, human fashionistas. The catwalk belongs to the cats this fall!

items.title: CEO mass emails employees, telling them which candidates to vote for: 'My coworkers and I are outraged.'
items.text:
Your CEO can tell you to do a lot of things. They can tell you when to show up to work in the morning and when you can leave. They can dictate what you wear to the office. Some of them even control whether or not you have a lunch break. While it's pretty normal for a CEO to dictate what you do at work, it's more unusual to tell your employees what to do outside of the office.

And yet, thousands of employers from sea to shining sea tell their employees they aren't allowed to post certain things on social media or express certain views publicly if they want to keep working for the company. And whether you like it or not, a company is entitled to do that! 49 out of the 50 states in the United States have at-will employment, which means an employer can fire an employee at any time, for any reason (or no reason at all), and without prior notice, as long as the reason for termination is not illegal. It would be illegal to fire somebody for being from a different country, because National Origin is one of the protected classes in the United States. A Swiftie CEO can fire an employee for posting a tirade on social media about how much they hated Taylor Swift, because being a Swiftie is not a protected class. I know it sounds ridiculous, but it's true!

Many Americans don't understand that the 1st Amendment doesn't protect you from getting fired for what you say. It protects you from going to jail for what you say. For example, your boss could fire you if you openly insult his character during a meeting, but he can't send you to jail for that. While he might try to sue you for slander, the case would probably get thrown out due to lack of evidence of harm

We all know that employees are limited by what they can say, lest they lose their jobs, but what about CEOs? Company shareholders are often the only people who can control what CEOs do, as they're the only people who can really force them to step down. They might be the only people who can tell a CEO that it's not a great idea to tell their employees who to vote for, but clearly the shareholders of the company in this story don't care that their CEO told employees to do that, or agree with him doing it.

items.title: The 20 Best Friendship Memes of The Week (November 4, 2026)
items.text:
Don't you ever feel like your friends are the only thing keeping you sane in the incredible mess that is your life?

Friendship can mean very different things depending on who you ask. Some people see it as people they like to hang out with meeting up, other see them as family members, siblings from other parents, and others just as a relationship that was cultivated so long ago that even when they don't see each other it's still there. No matter what your take on friendship, we all have at least a friend in the world. It may not be the kind of relationship where you see each other more than once a week and know everything about each other to the point that you don't have any more things to talk about. It may just be the kind of friendship that can go months and even years without sending each other a message, but when you see each other, it's like time has never gone by. You may be apart in a physical way, but never in a sentimental one.

Some people seem to be very judgy about where you met your friends, saying things like "you can't be friends with your coworkers". That's not true. You can be friends with whoever you want. Sometimes your best friend is your childhood friend who grew up with you, and your families are like one big family. But other times it's just someone you met in line in the grocery store and hit it off with, or maybe someone that you used to encounter at the beauty salon, or even someone you met through an ex-partner. Anything can lead to you cultivating a friendship; the important thing is not how, but with whom. That person you like enough to consider them a friend.

We use the word 'friend' as if it meant something, as if anyone and everyone were our friend, but that is simply impossible. A friend is much more than just someone you know. It's someone you love, you respect, you appreciate. Someone who has no reason to be by your side, as they are not family, nor do they want to marry you, but they still want to be a part of your life. You and that person have an incredible link that could be impossible to understand by anyone else. A friend is not 'just a friend '; a friend is like a non-romantic soulmate, a forever link that grew out of compatibility in the strongest ways. So stop saying "they are just a friend"; the "just" makes it seem like they matter less as your friend, and it should be the other way around. They are your friend, and that is more than enough. So start appreciating your friends as they deserve it. It's one of the most important relationships you could ever have, so stop underestimating the link between two good friends. It can be stronger than you have ever thought, sometimes even stronger than romantic relationships.

items.title: A Charcuterie Board of 25+ Cheese Memes From Cheddar to Gouda and Everything in Between
items.text:
If you told me I could never have cheese again, I would need to take several weeks off of work in order to mourn.

Cheese is the bedrock of a life well lived, if you ask me. Melt a slice of it on a sandwich, and I'm a happy camper. Drench a slice of pizza in it, and I am smiling ear to ear. Set out a cheese board with an array of different selections, paired with some nice breads, jams, and pickles… I am as close to heaven as I will ever be on Earth. This is just my truth. I've rarely met a cheese that I didn't like. I appreciate it in all forms, whether it be stinky or spicy or creamy or goat. Bring it on, and leave me alone with it for a while.

items.title: 25+ Redhead Memes for 'National Love Your Red Hair Day' (November 5, 2026)
items.text:
Redheads get so many mixed messages about their hair color. One day, they're being told that they're the most beautiful people in the world, and the next day some snot-nosed brat is quoting Eric Cartman and telling them that they have no souls. It's hard to know how to feel about your red hair in a world that feels so conflicted about it, but today is a day of celebration!

South Park has done irreparable damage to the redheaded community for the past two decades. Before the infamous episode Ginger Kids, red-haired kids were subjected to harassment from their peers about their hair color, but not for their lack of souls. After Cartman proudly spouted the idea that ginger kids have no souls, Pandora's box was opened. In 2008, members of a Facebook group called "Kick a Ginger" tried to start a "National Kick a Ginger Day."

But let's be honest: there has been discrimination against people with red hair far before South Park ever did it. In the Middle Ages, red hair and green eyes were thought to be a sign of somebody being a witch, werewolf, or vampire. Redheads are thought to have a fiery temper that matches their hair color, as Anne in Anne of Green Gables was described. Redheads also had the stereotype of being libidinous.

These negative stereotypes are why "National Love Your Red Hair Day" matters! Stephanie and Adrienne Vendetti, two redheaded sisters who founded the brand How To Be a Redhead, established the holiday, and some of their very own memes are included in this redhead meme list!

items.title: Boyfriend demands 26-year-old actress girlfriend to turn down the lead in a musical because she has an onstage kiss: 'He’s acting as if I’m being selfish for not turning it down'
items.text:
When someone doesn't take your career seriously, that can be a pretty big relationship red flag.

Just because someone's career is a little less traditional doesn't mean that it's not a real career. I've dealt with this plenty of times in my life. I've taken a somewhat less traditional path, and sometimes I feel myself having to justify it to someone else. But the thing is, your life is your life, and you're the only one who has to live it. As long as you're making choices to feed yourself, you're in the clear. I feel like this often happens to people who pursue careers in the arts. There is not always a straight line you can draw between career moves when you're in the arts. Sometimes it looks way more like a jagged line. There are ups and downs and survival jobs and moves that might not make sense to anyone else. And it may seem like "less important" work than other jobs out there, but the arts are deeply important, and the folks pursuing them should be taken seriously. It's a career, after all, and a difficult one at that. The woman in this story was in the thick of that misunderstanding, and her boyfriend wasn't giving a lot of leeway.

When you're an actor, onstage or on-camera intimacy is part of the job. It's hard to limit yourself to roles where you don't have to do that, and it's an important part of acting. But some folks outside of the industry don't totally understand that, and read too much into it. In my mind, it's acting. It's not real intimacy; it's a highly choreographed scene that two characters are playing. Especially onstage, in a musical. These things are hammered down to the last detail. They're not exactly romantic. The boyfriend in this story didn't quite understand that, though.

items.title: Woman donates partner's designer clothes to local shelter after discovering he's leading a double life: ‘I uncovered a second social media, apartment, and relationship’

items.title: 'Happiness is a warm puppy': Animal laughs and joys for a happy brain giving your midweek slump a silly paw pick-me-up (November 4, 2026)
