What do you do when you get home after a long, stressful day? Everybody has their own way of unwinding, but animal lovers can all agree: snuggling up to your beloved pet will bring you back to life in an instant. This isn't just because they're so cute and fuzzy, though that does help. It is also because of the connection you have with your pets.

Other than the fact that humans have been meticulously raising certain animals to physically appear how we want them to and be useful in ways we need them, there is something else there. It's something magical that is inexplicable to science, other than that we somehow release the same sort of chemicals a mother and child have to bond when we see our furbabies. But why does that happen? Well, we don't really know. We just love our furbabies so much that they truly feel like our born-from-our-womb babies. So when we see them, oxytocin is released, and you bond with your pet and love them more and more every day. Unfortunately, we have to go to work and do things that take us away from our beloved pets. So let's look at relatable memes and feel happy and grateful that you have someone excited to see you when you get home.

items.title: Business owner asks job applicant to shadow the employee he is replacing and not tell her that he's her replacement: 'She has been there for 11 years.'
items.text:
The job interviewing process is the perfect time to suss out red flags in a company before you commit to working for them. If a job is giving you a bad feeling before you even sign on, that might be the universe telling you that it is not the right job for you.

When you conduct a job interview, look for red flags in the people you're interviewing. If they say, "My last boss was so horrible" before they say anything else, that is a huge red flag. I know a lot of people don't agree with judging somebody for saying that in a job interview, but I think it's worth judging somebody for it. First of all, it's common sense that you shouldn't be complaining about anything in a job interview. Who wants to work with someone who complains about everything all the time? I know I sure don't! There is also a good chance their previous workplace wasn't as bad as they claim, and they're actually the problem. How many times have you heard of somebody in your life complaining about their "crazy ex" or their "bad roommate," only for you to realize later on that they were 100% the bad partner or bad roommate?

The interviewer isn't the only one who gets to judge. Maybe as the interviewee, you decide you wouldn't want to work somewhere that would judge you for bringing iced coffee into the job interview, so you bring iced coffee to the job interview to filter out the employers you'd rather not work for. It's totally okay to reject a job offer if half the interview is spent with the interviewer claiming this job is for hard workers willing to go the extra mile, because you know that is code for, "you will never get to go home before 8 PM ever again." It's better to reject a job that seems suspicious from the jump than to feel stuck there because you don't want to look like a job hopper.

items.title: The Best Celebrity Halloween Costumes of 2026
items.text:
Was your Halloween costume better than the one these celebrities wore? Was it better than Heidi Klum's?

If you like Halloween and celebs, you definitely know about Heidi Klum and the insane costumes she has worn through the years. To me, I have to admit that she has become a little obsession of mine, especially after the worm costume. Every year, on Halloween night, I'm always expectant to see what incredible outfit she is going to pull out, and she never disappoints! If you are not familiar with her game, let me tell you about some of the costumes she has done in the last few years.

Heidi Klum has been dressing up for Halloween in this out of the top costume for 25 years now. She knows what she is doing, but she also has the craziest ideas. If I had to pick my favorites, I would start with the one from 2013 where she dressed as a senior-citizen version of herself. Another one that I love is the one from 2015 when she dressed up as Jessica Rabbit from Who Framed Roger Rabbit? She wore a lot of prosthetics that fully sold the image of a real-life version of the character. In 2016, she did the simplest costume she could do, but it was no less than iconic. This year, she topped herself doing what seems to be my favorite Halloween costume, competing with the worm from 2022, of course. She decided to get dressed as a hand. When I say hand, I mean an anatomically correct hand with nerves and bones coming out of the wrist where it was cut from the rest of the body, and several rings on the "fingers". She is not the only celebrity who dresses up for Halloween, but we must admit she is the most committed to the bit. She doesn't care how many hours she has to sit in a makeup chair. There were other amazing costumes worn this Halloween by your favorite celebrities, but let's just be honest: no one was even near topping her. We have to give flowers where flowers are due. items.title: Mother-in-law demands family celebrate Christmas morning at her house so her 14-year-old son gets presents from Santa, DIL insists: ‘He's too old to believe in Santa’

To be fair, it truly is impossible not to fight about the where, when, and who's of the holidays, since each person in the family wants their version of a perfect holiday, and they rarely align with the expectations of other people around them. items.title: Veterinary student takes in a three-legged tuxedo cat with no plans to keep him, but one photo reveals just how much everything changed
items.text:
Every cat foster parent knows the danger of getting a little too attached. You bring home a kitty with the best intentions, promising yourself that you're only providing a temporary place to stay. A few weeks later, they've claimed your bed, stolen your heart, and somehow convinced you that your home would be incomplete without them. Oops!

Foster fails are practically a tradition in the cat-loving community. After all, how are you supposed to say goodbye to a little fluffball who's spent weeks following you around, demanding cuddles, and becoming part of your daily routine? Those tiny paws have a remarkable talent for making themselves right at home.

For one veterinary student, however, adopting a cat was never part of the plan. Their studies, finances, and future career moves made permanent pet ownership seem unrealistic. When a rescued tuxedo cat named Clay entered their life, they intended to help him recover before eventually returning him to the streets.

Clay had already been through an awful ordeal, losing a paw after suffering a severe wound. He needed care and a safe place to recover, and his temporary human was determined to help.

What they hadn't anticipated was how much they'd need him, too.

Three years later, Clay is still by their side, and the two are practically inseparable. He's an affectionate little gentlecat who loves cuddling and insists on staying close to his human throughout the day.

We all know the joy of coming home to a pet who's happy to see us. Even the most exhausting day feels a little easier when there's a furry companion waiting to curl up beside you. Clay's human says they wouldn't even want to come home if he weren't there.

Clay also extends his kindness to the other animals his human helps. He's especially gentle with incoming foster cats, even meowing at nervous newcomers as though he's reassuring them.

Clay has faced more than his fair share of challenges, including a painful dental condition that required extensive treatment. His human was so emotional about leaving him in veterinary care that they called their mom for support.

The student initially worried that a permanent pet would be too much to handle. Instead, Clay became their favorite part of coming home.

He may have lost a paw, but this sweet tuxedo boy has certainly gained a whole lot of love.

items.title: November Memes for All People Who Can't Believe How Fast The Year Is Going by and That We're Almost In Holiday Season

items.title: ‘What's the most unbelievable excuse someone gave for being late, but later turned out to be true?’: People discuss the most crazy excuses they have heard that turned out to be true
items.text:
The excuse may sound crazy, but that doesn't mean that it isn't true!

Excuses: what your manager says every time you explain yourself. Unfortunately, people are so used to lying and hearing lies that now, when you try to explain yourself, what happened, or your behavior, everyone thinks it's just another excuse. I get it; sometimes some of them are pretty hard to believe. As a teacher, you won't believe that the student's homework was eaten by their dog. As a boss, you will not believe that the email talking badly about you wasn't written by the person who sent it. As a cashier, you won't believe that the client forgot their wallet, but they will come right back with the money to pay. That's how life works. Some excuses have been used way too much; now no one will believe they are true. But sometimes, and just sometimes, they are true. The person who you are looking at thinking, "How can they think I will believe that" it's actually telling you the truth. But hey, it's hard to prove it.

This happened to me one time, and it was so hard to make my friend understand that it wasn't just a fake excuse. A couple of years back, I was on a bus going from the train station to a special class that was not at school; it was at a museum. I got on the bus at the perfect time to arrive early, which is not normal for me. But it was an important day; I needed to be on time. The bus was around midway when, all of a sudden, it broke down. A bummer, but that is not uncommon. I still had time to wait for the next bus and still arrive on time. I texted a friend telling her that, just in case I'm not there at 5, my bus broke down, but I won't be more than 5 minutes late. I waited until another bus comes in, I go up, take my seat, and off to go again. Not even 20 blocks away, the bus broke down. I'm not kidding! I realized I must be having a bad luck day or something.

When I finally made it to the museum, I was 30 minutes late. My friend couldn't believe that I was on two buses and that both broke down. She said I was inventing that because I'm always late. And that is true; I'm always late, but that time I wasn't. Luckily, my professor believed me, so after class he asked me to stay a bit longer so he could tell me what had happened when I was on the bus.

My story was just a fake excuse to my friend, and it was almost impossible for her to believe me. But well, I understand her. I'm always late, and two buses breaking down in the middle of the street isn't a normal thing that happens every day. At least I didn't miss the full class, and my professor was understanding about the whole crazy day I had.

items.title: The Chronicles of Cat Memes for Nostalgic Adults Missing the Magic of Childhood (November 1, 2026)
items.text:
November is a month of solemn surprises, and changes in weather. These cat memes remind us that our childhoods aren't as far away as we may think.

There's something about November that I just love. I love the word itself; the word November comes from the Latin word novem, which means nine. So why is the 11th month of the year named 9? It's because in the ancient Roman calendar, the year began in spring with March instead of January. But around 713 BC, a Roman King added January and February to the beginning of the year, thus pushing November to the eleventh position. A little bit of history when no one asked for it! In the Old English Name for November, some called November Blōtmōnaþ, which meant a month of sacrifice for the preparations of winter. I guess there's something about the beginning movements into winter that make me excited, and also make me feel nostalgic.

Our childhoods are within us whether we want to realize it or not. Sometimes, everything in our lives subconsciously go back to our childhoods, and that's not a bad thing. And there's something bittersweet about growing up and realizing childhood is getting further and further away from you. The world which once felt enormous, enchanted, magical, and full of mysteries becomes flat, bland, or grey with adult lenses that blur the magic. But with cat memes it doesn't go away! With cat memes that kind of unexplored kingdom of majesty and magic is still there because cats are just as innocent as children. The first day of November is something to celebrate. The magic doesn't disappear, sometimes we just forget where to look for it.

items.title: ‘Me: So I met this new guy… My tarot cards: 👹’: 17 Classical Art Memes for Timeless Relatability
items.text:
When tarot cards tell you he is the Devil, and he actually is

I love it when you ask the universe for a sign, and the sign is so clear that it's a little embarrassing.

Last week, I was about to go on a date with a guy that I had my doubts about. I drew a card from the deck before stepping out the door, and the card was the Devil, lol. Obviously, I don't base my decisions on what the tarot says, but I thought it was pretty funny that three hours later I was trying to figure out how to escape an awful date with a very problematic person.

Of course, a card like that can signify a lot of things; it can mean obsession, temptation, liberation, and many other things if you analyze it deeply enough. But sometimes I wonder if that's not giving the card too much credit for its symbolic complexity. Maybe it was only supposed to mean that the guy was, to put it plainly, evil.

Luckily, I went on only one date with him. I feel like the teenage me would've found it hard to say no to a kiss or to a second date, but right now my program is strict. I have no reason to be complacent. I didn't like the guy, and I found his vibe off-putting; that's enough reason not to give him a kiss or to go on a second date, even if my impressions were unfounded (which I know they aren't, but anyway).

I feel so happy that I can dodge a bullet so quickly nowadays. I don't need a three-month situationship and a lot of unnecessary drama to reach that point these days. To recognise a bad idea before it unfolds is a skill that I've developed over time.

Going back to tarot, and ignoring how it supposedly relates to magic. I like the potential it has to bring up things that we're already sensing. I don't think what we interpret from an ambivalent image is innocent at all; it is always influenced by what already exists as content in our minds, and that can be used to our advantage if we learn to see it.

That is also why I kinda love the classical art memes I upload every Sunday. There is something endlessly entertaining about taking something that was created hundreds of years ago and finding new meaning in it.

To me, it just further proves that images are polysemic and that we interpret them depending on what's populating our minds at a specific moment. We do this not only individually but collectively as well. We assign meaning to images depending on historical context. I know this is all objectively obvious, but I feel like it's interesting to revisit from time to time.

So next time you're about to go on a date with someone and feel a little ambivalent about them, please draw a tarot card and let projection do the rest! You won't be disappointed.

items.title: Son's girlfriend is graduating, and his mom got invited, she wanted to go, but with a friend, girlfriend didn't like the idea, now the mom wants to cancel: 'I let them both live with me for the past four years, and this is how I am treated'
items.text:
If you are invited somewhere, one should always assume that only you are invited, not you and whoever you want to bring as well.

Imagine graduating and deciding to invite your boyfriend's mother to the celebration, as you live with her, and she was helpful during the time you were studying, only to find out she wants to bring a friend with her under the pretense that she doesn't want to feel left out with your family, even though her son will be there. Now imagine that you are being invited to your son's girlfriend's graduation party that is far away, so you want to bring a friend to stay with you and do things together that do not include the graduation party, as this person is not invited to that. Are you lost? So are the people from this story. This is such a huge misunderstanding that can only be blamed on the lack of communication skills that people have. Did you notice that both things could occur at the same time without bothering anyone? Let me explain.

To be clearer, I'm going to call the boyfriend's mother Jane. So, to get the context of the non-issue: the girlfriend wants Jane to come to her out-of-town graduation. Jane wants to go, but she doesn't want to stay with the girlfriend's family, so she wants to bring a friend with her to split the Airbnb. Where's the issue, you may be asking? The girlfriend doesn't want Jane´s friend at the graduation ceremony, but that was not going to happen. The problem is that Jane said she wanted to bring a friend but never explained that it would only be to stay with her, not to accompany her to the ceremony. So is there really an issue? I don't think so. The real problem in all this is that these two people aren't communicating clearly and are using the boy they have in common as a cellphone. If they had talked to each other, they would soon realize that both things they want can happen at the same time without creating any problems.

My takeaway from all this is that people need to talk to each other more. Stop texting, for once and for all, and call someone to arrange something like this. If you are planning something important, you shouldn't be handling it with text messages. Go to their house and talk to them or call them like in the old times. Writing everything can lead to misunderstandings; not everyone understands what they want. That's why you call them. New generations love to text for everything. If they could send an emoji or sticker that explained everything, they would. Well, stop that. Talk over the phone like a normal person would, and all these misunderstandings would end pretty quickly. So next time you enter an argument like this one, remember me and call the other person. I promise you everything will be easier to sort out once you get used to talking to people that way.

items.title: 25 Cat Memes to Bring Back Childhood Magic and Simpler Days

items.title: 3 mountain lion cubs rescued on separate occasions become the cutest bonded trio, proving family is sometimes found, not just born

When rescued big cats cannot be released back into the wild, the most important thing is helping them find new purpose.

Mountain lions, and really big cats in general, are some of the most fascinating animals out there. As adults, they're powerful and graceful, capable of navigating enormous territories and thriving in the wild. But as cubs? Rescuing big cats isn't just about saving their lives, it's about giving these incredible big cats a chance to thrive and find new purpose in their new and different lives.

items.title: ‘Sometimes, I want to be treated mean. Just a little, though’: 10 Animal Crossing Conversations That Made the Game Extra Philosophical
items.text:
Unexpected Philosophy in Animal Crossing

I think Animal Crossing is the perfect scenario to have philosophical conversations. I don't know what it is, but there is something about an animal wearing a cute little sweater and walking around an island doing nothing that prompts philosophical contemplation.

Maybe it's the similarity to what we know about the ancient Greek lifestyle, or at least what we think we know about it. Or maybe it's the estrangement from ordinary life that a place like the virtual world offers. But, undoubtedly, Animal Crossing stimulates all sorts of uncanny and involuntarily wise conversations.

The characters don't have jobs or pressing responsibilities, and just like our unemployed friends or cousins, they have a lot of time to think about transcendent matters. Also, when you're talking to somebody else through a character, you tend to be a lot more uninhibited and even witty, so the format sure helps.

The contrast between the scale of their observations, their bluntness, and the cuteness of the animals' appearances will forever be funny to me. Someone will tell you something that sounds like it's been taken straight out of a Shakespeare novel and then ask you to bring them three pieces of fruit; it cracks me up every time.

Animal Crossing is like a constant Sunday. You spend the entire day rearranging flowers and talking to neighbours, and that seems to be a valid lifestyle around there. I love it, and I wish real life were a little more like that. They said we should dream big, right?

Each villager has their own personality and quirks, just like humans and Sims do. They can be ridiculous at one moment and surprisingly insightful a couple of seconds after.

I literally remember more Animal Crossing dialogue than phrases my friends have told me in real life, but maybe that's just because I'm crazy and I love the game. This particular weekend, I'm trying my best to go out and not stay in playing video games the entire time because it's clearly no good for me; we'll see how that goes.

I'm hoping that if a cartoon duck can make you reconsider your relationship with time, a real person can say something as insightful in a random bar on a Saturday. At least I have to go out in the sun for a while; this excessive computer usage is driving me crazy.

My screen time is through the roof lately, so even though I remember Animal Crossing very fondly, I cannot play it right now. I'm definitely going to play it when I deserve a virtual treat, but I swear I don't deserve it right now. I deserve to touch grass, and I know that is not a bad thing. It's just that I've gotten used to staying inside.

After all, I'm not an Animal Crossing character; I have pressing responsibilities and human needs to take care of. I can't spend my days rearranging virtual flowers and talking to strange creatures even though I want to.

Oh, how I miss you, Animal Crossing!

items.title: Little Legs and Big Sploot Energy From Cats Who Know How to Get Comfortable.
items.text:
Cats have a reputation for being graceful, elegant creatures, but that reputation goes right out the window when they decide to sploot. Suddenly, your majestic little house tiger is lying belly-down on the floor with their back legs stretched out like a pair of furry chicken drumsticks. So much for feline sophistication!

If you've never heard of splooting, it's the adorable position cats sometimes take when they stretch their hind legs out behind them while lying on their bellies. It's a wonderfully ridiculous sight, especially when your usually dignified kitty suddenly resembles a fluffy little frog.

Anyone who lives with a cat knows they're basically made of liquid. They'll squeeze into impossibly small boxes, twist themselves into bizarre sleeping positions, and somehow fit their entire bodies inside a bathroom sink. Splooting is just another entry on the long list of feline poses that make us question whether cats have any bones at all.

The classic sploot features both back legs stretched straight behind the kitty, leaving them looking like a furry pancake with drumsticks. Other cats prefer the half sploot, with just one leg sticking out to the side. It's a pretty impressive display of flexibility for an animal whose main daily responsibilities involve napping, eating, and knocking things off tables.

Cats might sploot to stretch their muscles, relax, or enjoy a cool spot on the floor. Whatever their motivation, their humans are almost guaranteed to stop whatever they're doing and admire those ridiculous little legs. Good luck walking past a splooting kitty without taking at least one picture.

Meanwhile, the cat couldn't care less about all the attention. Their humans are practically crying with laughter over the sight of those tiny drumsticks, and the kitty is just lying there wondering why everyone is making such a fuss. Excuse us, but you're shaped like a pancake with legs. How are we supposed to act normal?

Some cats take their splooting talents to another level. They'll stretch out across the hallway, flatten themselves against the kitchen tiles, or claim the middle of the living room floor like they're posing for a feline yoga magazine. Apparently, the entire house is their purrsonal stretching studio.

Whether they're showing off a full sploot, a half sploot, or a pose that defies explanation, these flexible felines are proof that cats can make even lying on the floor ridiculously entertaining.

Long live the sploot and all those adorable little kitty drumsticks!

items.title: Daughter demands mom cook Thanksgiving dinner and transport it to her house although she won't be attending the meal, husband protests when she refuses: 'It just seems impractical'
items.text:
Why should she have to do all the work when she isn't even the host?

Being the person who takes on hosting duties for the holidays is a huge responsibility, but there are a lot of people who seem to do everything in their power not to treat it that way. Recent statistics suggest that the proportion of households inviting over family or friends at least once a month has fallen over 30% since the 70s. It is very easy to blame all kinds of modern ills for this decline, but one of the reasons is undeniably that it is a big commitment! The cooking, cleaning, and entertaining all add up to a significant amount of time and effort.

Of course, it can be well worth it for the payoff that is enjoying spending time together. It's just important that the work involved gets properly recognized. This is a big part of the reason that countless families face drama surrounding who hosts and who does what to contribute. If somebody is expected to do everything all the time without being given an alternative option, there is every chance that they will become resentful.

While having that relative who creates the family holiday traditions can be wonderful, there also comes a time when others should think about taking over or at least relieving some of the burden. items.title: Woman hears desperate cries while walking her dog and rescues a tiny kitten who ends up falling for her fiancé instead
items.text:
There's nothing quite like the betrayal of a cat choosing someone else as their favorite person. You feed them, clean their litter box, buy them expensive toys, and spend half your paycheck making sure they're happy. Meanwhile, someone who barely lifts a finger gets all the cuddles. The audacity!

You could spend hours trying to win over a shy kitty, only for them to march straight past you and curl up on someone else's lap. Apparently, all that hard work means nothing when a cat has already made up their mind.

One cat lover recently experienced this firsthand after an unexpected rescue mission during a routine dog walk. They were outside their apartment complex when they heard a kitten screaming and spotted something darting underneath the parked cars.

After bringing their dog inside, they returned to investigate and discovered a frightened kitten hiding beneath someone's van. Luckily, they already had a cat at home, so they grabbed some wet food and headed back outside. The little kitty wasn't particularly interested in making things easy. She kept running between cars, forcing her rescuer to follow her around the parking lot before finally getting close enough to offer food.

Once she started eating, they carefully picked her up, expecting a struggle. Surprisingly, the kitten didn't fight back and allowed herself to be carried indoors. We can only imagine the relief of finally catching that little escape artist. Trying to rescue a frightened kitten from underneath parked cars sounds like quite the workout, especially when your original plans involved nothing more exciting than walking the dog.

Back inside, the rescuer fed the kitten and set up a comfortable spot for her in the bathroom. Their fiancé was at work, completely unaware that another furry family member had joined the household.

After everything the rescuer had done, you'd think the kitten would be purrmanently attached to their side. Nope! The little troublemaker decided the fiancé was her favorite person instead.

The rescuer admitted to being a little jealous, which is completely understandable. Imagine doing all the work and watching someone else collect the cuddles!

Two weeks later, the kitten, now named Shadow, is settling into her new home alongside the family's resident orange cat, Tigger. Shadow might have questionable taste in favorite humans, but at least she knows a good home when she finds one!

items.title: College student finishes her midterms and gets the sweetest surprise when her brother texts her about a black kitten who needs a home
items.text:
October is black cat season. They're everywhere on Halloween decorations, perched beside pumpkins, and featured in every witchy movie imaginable. But finding an actual black kitten in your backyard during spooky season? That's a Halloween surprise most cat lovers would have a hard time turning down.

Black cats have spent centuries dealing with silly superstitions about bad luck, which is especially unfair considering how adorable they are. We'd argue that finding one is pretty lucky, particularly when that little kitty needs someone to take them in. Forget four-leaf clovers. We'd happily take a miniature house panther any day.

One college student recently got an unexpected opportunity to welcome a little Halloween magic into their life. They'd just finished their midterms when they noticed messages from both their brother and sister-in-law. Since neither usually texted without a reason, the double notification was suspicious.

The mystery was solved when both sent pictures of a black kitten who had apparently been dumped in their yard.

The student and their boyfriend immediately gathered a crate, bought kitten food, and headed over to collect him. No elaborate planning or weeks of debating whether they were ready for another pet. There was a kitten who needed a home, and they were going to get him.

We love how quickly cat people can mobilize when there's a kitten involved. Getting someone to agree on dinner plans might take three days and seventeen messages, but mention a homeless kitten and suddenly everyone's ready to leave the house.

The couple already had a cat, which meant their newest family member would have to win over more than just his humans. Cats can be pretty particular about sharing their territory, especially when a stranger suddenly arrives expecting access to all the good napping spots.

Two weeks later, their resident kitty is finally starting to come around to the newcomer. Hopefully, the household will soon have two little partners in crime instead of one suspicious cat wondering who invited the new guy.

The kitten has officially been named Momo, and he's settling into life with his new family.

It's a lovely ending to what could have been a difficult situation for an abandoned little cat. Instead of spending October alone outdoors, Momo has people who went out of their way to bring him home.

Who needs Halloween candy when you can get a whole black kitten instead?

items.title: A Meowgical Halloween Full of Spooky Kitties, Purranormal Activity, and Feline Frights
items.text:
Happy Meowlloween, fellow cat lovers! The spookiest day of the year has officially arrived, and our feline friends are more than ready to celebrate. With their glowing eyes, mysterious nighttime activities, and occasional tendency to stare at invisible things, cats have always had a little Halloween spirit in them. Some might even argue that they're the reason haunted houses exist in the first place.

Black cats are practically the mascots of Halloween, thanks to centuries of witchy legends and spooky superstitions. But anyone who's shared a home with one knows that these little creatures of the night are usually more interested in treats than tricks. They might look like a powerful witch's familiar sitting in the window, but they're probably just watching a bird and wondering when dinner will be served.

Halloween costumes are a whole different kind of magic. There's nothing quite like seeing a kitty dressed as a tiny vampire, a fluffy pumpkin, or a miniature witch. Some cats seem perfectly happy to show off their spooky outfits, while others look ready to put a curse on their hoomans for even suggesting it. A cat in a witch hat might be adorable, but the expression underneath can be downright terrifying.

The decorations aren't safe from feline mischief, either. Dangling cobwebs make excellent toys, pumpkins are meant for sitting on, and those carefully arranged Halloween displays are just waiting for a curious paw to come along. Your home might be decorated for a night of spooky fun, but your cat has other plans. By the time they're finished, you'll have enough purranormal activity to keep the whole neighborhood entertained.

The real feline frights tend to happen when the lights go out. A mysterious crash in the kitchen, a shadow darting across the hallway, or a pair of glowing eyes staring at you from the darkness can turn an ordinary night into a full-blown horror movie. The culprit is usually a perfectly innocent-looking kitty who has absolutely no intention of explaining themselves.

Halloween wouldn't be quite as fun without these little monsters adding their own brand of chaos. From fangtastic expressions to spooky poses and plenty of cattitude, cats have a special talent for making even the scariest holiday ridiculously adorable.

So grab some candy, give your little monster a few extra treats, and enjoy a Halloween filled with purrs, paws, and just the right amount of hissteria.

items.title: 22 Household Chores Memes for Adults Spending Their Day Off Cooking, Cleaning, Doing Laundry and Cooking Again and Doing the Dishes and...
items.text:
Is sharing the housework enough if one person still has to plan everything?

I live alone, so dividing the housework is a very short conversation. I mean, there is no conversation. It's all mine. I do the laundry, I clean and handle everything else, and I'm also the person who has to remember what needs doing. Before I can wash anything, I need detergent. Before I can buy detergent, I need to notice I'm running out. No one thinks about all the thinking behind housework tasks. We often think about the physical workload and the visible results like a clean room or clean clothes.

That's why this University of Queensland paper caught my attention. Researchers studied heterosexual couples and divided household work into three kinds of loads: physical, cognitive and emotional. The physical load is doing the chores, the visible ones like cooking, cleaning, or doing home repairs. The cognitive load is the thinking and planning behind those activities. Who's going to do this? When? How? Do we need to buy something? So basically, cooking dinner means figuring out what to cook, how to get the ingredients you need, and planning how that will happen. There's much more effort than what we tend to think when we see the prepared meal as a result. Finally, the emotional load includes noticing how every household member feels and offering care.

And you know what? To absolutely no one's surprise, women reported having a greater contribution in all three areas.

items.title: Woman goes to throw away the garbage and finds a little kitten who walks right up to her, leading to an unexpected addition to the family
items.text:
There's a running joke among cat owners that you don't actually adopt cats. You just find them in the most random places and somehow end up taking them home. Under cars, behind dumpsters, in parking lots, or occasionally right inside the trash. The Cat Distribution System apparently has no interest in making the adoption process particularly glamorous.

We've seen plenty of stories about people going out to run a simple errand and returning with a new feline family member. You might leave the house to buy groceries, take a walk, or throw away the garbage, only to find yourself responsible for a little creature who now expects three meals a day and unlimited cuddles. Apparently, that's just how cat ownership works.

One couple recently experienced this firsthand when they went outside to throw away their trash and spotted a little fox-like kitten hanging around the communal bins. The poor baby was licking grease off discarded McDonald's packaging, desperately trying to find something to eat.

He was filthy, greasy, and clearly in need of help, but rescuing him was surprisingly easy. The kitten walked straight up to them and let them pick him up. With the nights getting colder, the couple decided to take him to the vet rather than leave him outside.

Unfortunately, the examination revealed that he'd been having a rough time. He was dehydrated, extremely hungry, and full of worms. The missing fur around his nose suggested he'd spent quite a while rummaging through garbage looking for food. He also had no microchip, and the vet was confident nobody was caring for him.

The couple already had a cat at home, so adopting another wasn't part of their plans. But after the kitten tested negative for FIV and received parasite treatments, they brought him home and settled him into a separate room.

Their resident cat has already started sniffing the newcomer through the gap beneath the door. We wonder what the poor kitty thinks about suddenly having a potential roommate. Imagine minding your own business when your humans return from taking out the trash with another cat!

The couple is still checking local Facebook groups in case someone is missing him, although they haven't found an owner. They've also spotted similar kittens nearby and suspect he may have been born outdoors earlier in the summer.

After a night indoors, the little guy was already enjoying a full belly and a warm blanket. It's a wonderful change for a kitten who'd been searching through garbage just hours earlier.

The Cat Distribution System strikes again, and this time, apparently, it offers curbside pickup.

items.title: ‘Level too Hard, Baba is Done, Better Look Out’: 13 Baba Is You Memes for the Intellectual Gamers
items.text:
Baba Is You: Like Solving Equations (Except It's Not Boring!)

I've been playing Baba Is You. For those who don't know it, it's a puzzle game that feels a little like solving equations, except they are made of words.

It seems really simple at first, but as you level up, you will likely find yourself stuck thinking really hard about how to solve the challenge.

The premise is simple: you control a little character named Baba that looks like a mouse or a capybara, and the rules of the game are written right there on the screen, like blocks of text that go: BABA IS YOU, WALL IS STOP, FLAG IS WIN. Those aren't only instructions about how the game works; they are buttons you can actually interact with.

If you move the words around and you form new phrases, you actually change what the rules of the game are.

For example, if the wall is closer to you, and you change the command from WALL IS STOP to WALL IS WIN, pushing the words around with Baba, and then you touch the flag using Baba again, you will win.

I know it sounds very simple, but it turns very complicated very fast.

The relationships between words and equivalences, and rules, are what remind me of equations. Language becomes both the problem and the way to solve it. Just like when you have an equation and you move numbers around and suddenly you clear x. Numbers were presented as a problem, and through some operations they became the solution.

I'm not sure I'm explaining my theory right, but that's how I feel about the game. Contrary to what people might think, it's very relaxing. Even though you're thinking most of the time, it's a different kind of thinking, and it gets you so concentrated that you forget your real-life problems completely.

Don't get me wrong, please; it doesn't feel like math homework. Please try it before making any assumptions. There is something so satisfying about solving a problem without looking at solutions and playing around with logic without feeling like we're back at school. At least that's the kind of game I love.

Baba Is You reminds me of Monkey Island, in the sense that you spend a lot of time looking for new combinations of stuff to get new results. It's not about doing it fast or dexterity; it's about logic and creativity.

Does anyone else in here like these kinds of games as well? I would describe them as games that stimulate your creative thinking and require you to constantly evolve your way of thinking about problems.

Anyway, I have to keep playing because even though I loved it, I haven't reached a super high level or anything. That's my new goal in life lol.

So, for those who already know and love Baba Is You, here is a compilation of memes to remember it fondly and to try to tempt you into going back to play it.

items.title: Family takes in a kitten from a feral colony to foster, but her bond with their son and Great Danes changes everything
items.text:
Fostering a kitten is supposed to be temporary. You give them a warm place to sleep, plenty of food, and lots of love until they're ready for their forever home. Unfortunately, nobody told little Agatha that she was only supposed to be staying for a few weeks.

When one family took in the tiny kitten, the plan was simple. Agatha had come from a feral cat colony and needed someone who could bottle-feed her and give her a safe place to grow. The family had fostered plenty of kittens before, so this wasn't exactly unfamiliar territory.

But there's a big difference between fostering an entire litter and caring for one tiny kitten. With a litter, the kittens have each other to play with and cuddle. When there's only one, you end up spending much more time holding, feeding, and bonding with them. That's a dangerous situation for anyone hoping to avoid another permanent pet.

Agatha also had some pretty convincing allies. The family's son took on overnight feeding and cleaning shifts, sometimes caring for her between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m. All that time together paid off, and the little kitten grew to absolutely adore and trust him. Looking at their pictures together, it's pretty clear the feeling is mutual.

She even managed to win over the family's Great Danes, joining them for afternoon naps. Considering how tiny Agatha is next to those enormous dogs, we can only imagine how comfortable she must be snuggled up beside them.

But the moment that really sealed the deal involved the family's husband. About two weeks after Agatha arrived, she was crying for her bottle when her foster mom heard him coming down the hallway, reassuring the kitten that Daddy was coming to get her.

Well, that's one way to announce you've become a cat dad.

By that point, it sounds like Agatha had already made herself at home. Between her devoted human brother, her giant canine cuddle buddies, and a dad who was completely wrapped around her tiny paw, there wasn't much reason for her to go anywhere else.

Now approximately nine weeks old, Agatha has officially graduated from foster kitten to permanent family member. The little former feral kitten has traded life outdoors for the comforts of being a thoroughly spoiled house princess.

But does this mean we have to stand for it? Tipping on something that you didn't even get service for is a pretty big ask. You have to wonder, who is it even going to? items.title: ‘Me at 11 PM After Eating Healthy All Day’: 17 Gym Memes for the Gym Bros Who Can’t Stop Eating Junk Food
items.text:
I Skipped the Gym for an Entire Week for the First Time in 10 Months. When does wanting to improve yourself become an inability to accept yourself as you are?

And suddenly it doesn't matter that I've been going consistently for a year and a half, that I always eat perfectly, or that even when I think I ate too much, I probably only ate 200 extra calories.

I know our bodies aren't supposed to be machines running at maximum capacity every day, but every time I miss a workout, the tiny voice in my head drives me crazy with questions.

For the past week or so, I haven't felt like going to the gym; that's it. It feels like a big deal in my mind, but it is really only that. I can't believe it has gotten to the point that if I skip a workout, I feel that I'm going to lose what I built over a year of working out. And if, on top of all that, I've been eating more carbohydrates, you can only imagine how I feel.

After this terrible experience, I've decided I'm not going to push myself this hard, and that I will give myself permission to stop and recharge when I need to. After all, I've proved myself time and time again that I'm not a quitter; there is no reason to worry that much.

Habits are built over time, and skipping the gym for a week doesn't suddenly erase the 500 weeks prior when you showed up. What began as an attempt to improve my quality of life can become another scenario where you scrutinize yourself, and that wasn't the point.

If rest is no longer rest, and it has become a pause from constant productivity: congratulations, you've succesfully trapped yourself. My new gym objective is that being active is just another thing that I do because I enjoy it and not something I constantly obsess about and that it runs my life.

Consistency is not the same as perfection. If I intend to do this for the rest of my life, I have to be able to accept some degree of ups and downs. I would like to reach the point in which I no longer stress about it, like I don't stress about taking showers or eating; it's just something that I do and that I will continue to do (hopefully) forever.

I will probably go back to the gym soon, when I feel ready, and I suppose I'm going to feel ready as soon as I stop treating the issue like a court summons. Until then, I will eat what my body tells me to eat, and if later this week I need to detox, I'm going to do it, but I will resist the urge to compensate for what I'm doing now.

The point of getting healthier was to enjoy life, not to find another way to suffer or feel guilty. Has any of you had this issue as well? Any tips to get over it?

items.title: Young man calls savings accounts 'dystopian,' questions why a 24-year-old with $5K wouldn't use that money to go to New York Fashion Week: 'It's more dystopian to not have savings.'
items.text:
It's pretty common for 24-year-olds to have nothing in savings. In fact, most 24-year-olds have a negative net worth from student loans or credit card debt, so any 24-year-old who has a positive net worth is something to celebrate. There is definitely such a thing as "living in the moment" too much, and if you willingly spend every penny you have on fun things, you're not going to be in a good position when you need your money for necessities.

There was a time in my life when I spent nearly every penny I made. I did always make sure to save a percentage of my income into my 401K, but that was easy! After all, it came directly out of my paycheck, and I didn't even have to think about it. But from ages 22 to 24, I basically spent all the money I made on whatever I wanted: Broadway tickets, basketball games, Citi Bike day passes, you name it! I just made sure I never let my bank account drop below a certain amount, so I wasn't spending more than I made, and that was good enough for me at the time!

As I've grown older, I've recognized the importance of saving more for my future. It's not enough to just save 10% of your check for retirement! You need an emergency fund of 3-6 months to cover unexpected expenses. You need to invest in the stock market so your money grows instead of sitting in a regular savings account forever. If you want to go on vacation, set up a "sinking fund" so you can save specifically for that, instead of draining your retirement account to go to a resort.

While some people are serious about saving money in their 20s, many aren't, even into their 30s, 40s, and 50s. Some adults with great jobs and kids still don't have $5,000 to their name, even though they make double that every month. When people have a high income but no savings, it points to a pattern of being undisciplined. If you can't delay pleasure and you buy everything you see, it's not a good sign for your long-term financial health.

It is pretty darn common for 24-year-olds to spend every dollar they have. The young man in this story is probably around that age, and he's learning that most people aren't as willing to spend their life savings as he is.

items.title: The 20 Best Friendship Memes of The Week
items.text:
I love my friends. They are the only people I can stand for more than two hours.

Friendships are one of the purest forms of love, and I stand on that hill. I always viewed friendship as the love that someone has for you even though they don't have to. Family is obliged to love you, and even then it's not always possible to accomplish. But friends don't. They don't owe you anything; they choose to love you. And to me, that is the purest way of love. So don't undermine your friends; they are people who choose to be by your side and want you to be the best person you can be.

At weddings, it is common for people who are close to the couple to say some words about them. I always like it when they move the family to the side for a little bit and let the friends talk. It doesn't matter if it's a childhood friend, a work friend, or someone you met two years ago in an elevator and became inseparable. They always have the most beautiful view of their friends. It's a vision that is untainted with expectations or family links. It's the view that shows that no matter what, they are there for each other, not because they have to, but because they really want to. And to me, that seems to have come out of a fairy tale. Yes, the mother of the bride knows her like the palm of her hand because she raised her and lived with her for years. But the friends learned everything about them by spending time together, and now they have noticed the little things that make the bride the person that she is.

Friendship is beautiful and pure, but it can also be toxic and tumultuous. But you know what? When your friendship is like that, it is because they aren't really your friend. When we were children, nobody taught us how to spot the people who want to take advantage of you or use you for something. On the contrary, we learn to always expect the best in people. Well, that wasn't really helpful. I'm not telling you that you need to be second-guessing everything and always assuming the worst, but you do need to trust your gut and be intelligent. If your "friend" is always trying to take you down or make you feel bad, then that isn't a true friendship; that is a toxic relationship that will only work to make you feel bad about yourself. You need to realize that and leave. We all deserve a friend who is nice and wants us to be the best version of ourselves, not someone who is praying for our downfall. So think about who your real friends are and prioritize them over others. They choose to be your friends because they love you, not because they want something in return. So be mindful and smart, and don't ever stay where you are not wanted for who you are.

items.title: 10 Halloween Costume Ideas for Couples
items.text:
Halloween is just around the corner, and you still haven't decided on a costume to do as a couple? You are lucky I got some ideas!

Halloween is my favorite holiday: everyone dressed up, kids trick-or-treating, amazing parties, cool photos, fun with friends. You cannot tell me it isn't better than Easter or Christmas. As I love Halloween, I am the perfect person to suggest costume ideas. Especially because this year I wanted to dress up with my boyfriend, and until we found something that worked for us, we reviewed every possible option. That's why I will present you with the 10 best and easiest costume ideas to do with someone else. And I will also tell you what I'm going as; maybe you can copy me if that's more your style.

The easiest costume ideas that I found for couples were definitely Joe and Love from the show You. It's especially easy. You just need one person dressed in an apron and holding a rolling pin, and the other dressed in black with a cap, and if you want to do it creepier, you can both splash yourselves with some red paint. It's easy to do, easy to understand, and easy to clean after. You don't need any crazy things, so it's also really cheap. Another good idea that is easy is Nick and Judy from Zootopia; it's a little cliché, I will admit. But that doesn't mean that it isn't good. You can either pick stuff from your closet and make it work by adding the ears and a tail, or you can buy a costume online, which is also pretty inexpensive.

If you can manage to do something a little bit more complicated, I would suggest doing Coraline and Wybie from Coraline. It's not that hard; the main things are the wig and the button eyes, but I get that wigs aren't for everyone. And if you are feeling like painting your whole body, I would really like to see at least one couple dress as Beast Boy and Raven from Teen Titans. It's so cool and not really that impossible. You just need to commit to the bit and paint yourself. It's not that bad.

I left more ideas below, but just in case you are curious about what I'm wearing to Halloween, I will be dressed as Misa Amane from Death Note, and, of course, my boyfriend will be dressed as Light Yagami. Yes, I know what you may be thinking: that isn't a love story, and I know. I just found the characters really interesting, and I thought it would be original to be dressed like them. After all, the idea of Halloween isn't for the costume to be perfect. It's more important to have fun with your friends or your partner and enjoy the scariest night of the year. Halloween is great whether you are dressed like a trash bag or as some great horror movie character. You just need to have the time of your life, and that is not dependent on your costume attire.

items.title: ‘The Memes Strike Back’: Star Wars memes for Rebels, Imperials and Force Users to Laugh at Across the Galaxy (October 28, 2026)
items.text:
There's a thought that doesn't leave my mind lately, and that is: how the heck did so many Jedi survive Order 66 and not come back to help?

It's funny to go back to the original movies from time to time and see how much easier everything would have been if they had only known that there were actually quite a few Jedi who survived and were scattered all over the galaxy. Imagine what it must have been like for Luke to stand up to both Darth Vader and Palpatine, given that he wasn't even alive when the Jedi Order still existed and never knew how they operated as a whole. If he had had another experienced Jedi by his side, the rebellion would have breathed a little more easily. Besides, by that time almost everyone seemed to have forgotten about the Jedi. Han Solo kept looking at Luke as if he were insane!

You could argue that Ahsoka and Kanan, who were still alive, weren't really Jedi. Ahsoka had left the Order, and Kanan never got to officially finish his training before starting to train Ezra, but at least they had seen how the original Jedi operated. Luke never did. Yoda did what he could to train Luke, and he did a good job, but still. Yoda was a great master, and Luke had it in his genes to be a good pupil, but it's not the same to have some training in a skill you had barely known existed and then off to save the world as it is to have more experienced people by your side to accompany you and give more insight. Still, Luke managed, and we love him for it.

items.title: DCU Memes for All DC Comics Fans Who Are Begging James Gunn to Deliver a Good Justice League Movie and Choose the Right Batman
items.text:
You can never please everybody, and anyone in the entertainment industry sure knows that better than anybody…

If you're like me, every time you set foot on the internet and see people complaining about stuff, specifically entertainment-related stuff, you wonder: What does it take to please an audience? Because, so far, not even movie directors have figured that out, especially not movie directors working on superhero projects.

After the release of Clayface, director James Gunn is defending his work, expressing the idea that not all stories within the same universe have to lead to the same outcome, and people on Twitter don't quite seem to agree with him, for whatever reason they have.

Gunn's work for his DCU has been compared since the beginning with Zack Snyder's vision for his own, and there are always mixed reactions. Some people praise him for having more variety of tone across the shows and movies of this new universe; others are happy that now the productions seem to have colors besides grey, and others believe Snyder's universe was more complex and better plotted. Some people thrash Gunn's movies and call them 'awful', asking that he be fired, saying that he's not a good director, and so on. However, if you look at the numbers, you'll see that his version of Superman has an 83% critics' acceptance on Rotten Tomatoes, and 90% from the audience. Lanterns has a 91% from the critics and a 67% from the people; Supergirl is the lowest, with a 52% from the critics, but a good 72% from fans. And so far, Clayface has been doing great, with a 75% from critics and a 94% from audiences.

If the general reception is good and reviews are positive, why are people so critical? Well, that has an easy answer: people like complaining. And that goes to show that whatever mean comments go online are not necessarily a reflection of what happens in reality. Numbers rarely lie, and if DC is keeping James Gunn in their projects, he must be doing something right.

items.title: 'He's twice the size of my other Sphynx cats': Couple adopts an 11-year-old giant Peterbald cat after his owners can no longer care for him, and he fills their house with hilarious chaos
